121:         self.entries[..self.len as usize]
122:             .iter()
123:             .rev()
124:             .find(|z| z.area.contains(pos))
125:             .copied()
126:     }
127:

129:         self.entries[..self.len as usize]
130:             .iter()
131:             .find(|z| z.zone == zone)
132:     }

141: /// Anchor + cursor in doc space. `area` and `zone` are captured at mouse-down
142: /// so layout changes mid-drag don't break the selection.
143: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
144: pub struct Selection {
145:     anchor: DocPos,
146:     cursor: DocPos,
147:     pub area: Rect,
148:     pub zone: SelectionZone,
149: }
150: 
151: fn screen_to_doc(screen_row: u16, area: Rect, scroll_offset: u32) -> u32 {
152:     let clamped = screen_row.clamp(area.y, area.y + area.height.saturating_sub(1));
153:     scroll_offset + (clamped - area.y) as u32
154: }
155: 
156: fn clamp_col(col: u16, area: Rect) -> u16 {
157:     col.clamp(area.x, area.x + area.width.saturating_sub(1))
158: }
159: 
160: impl Selection {
161:     pub fn start(row: u16, col: u16, area: Rect, zone: SelectionZone, scroll_offset: u32) -> Self {
162:         let doc_row = screen_to_doc(row, area, scroll_offset);
163:         let doc_col = clamp_col(col, area);
164:         let pos = DocPos::new(doc_row, doc_col);
165:         Self {
166:             anchor: pos,
167:             cursor: pos,
168:             area,
169:             zone,
170:         }
171:     }
172: 
173:     pub fn update(&mut self, row: u16, col: u16, scroll_offset: u32) {
174:         self.cursor = DocPos::new(
175:             screen_to_doc(row, self.area, scroll_offset),
176:             clamp_col(col, self.area),
177:         );
178:     }
179: 
180:     pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
181:         self.anchor == self.cursor
182:     }
183: 
184:     pub fn highlight_area(&self) -> Rect {
185:         match self.zone {
186:             SelectionZone::Messages => Rect::new(
187:                 self.area.x,
188:                 self.area.y,
189:                 self.area.width.saturating_sub(1),
190:                 self.area.height,
191:             ),
192:             _ => self.area,
193:         }
194:     }
195: 
196:     pub fn normalized(&self) -> (DocPos, DocPos) {
197:         if self.anchor <= self.cursor {
198:             (self.anchor, self.cursor)
199:         } else {
200:             (self.cursor, self.anchor)
201:         }
202:     }
203: 
204:     pub fn to_screen(self, scroll_offset: u32) -> Option<ScreenSelection> {
205:         let (start, end) = self.normalized();
206:         if start == end {
207:             return None;
208:         }
209: 
210:         let view_top = scroll_offset;
211:         let view_bottom = scroll_offset + self.area.height as u32;
212: 
213:         if end.row < view_top || start.row >= view_bottom {
214:             return None;
215:         }
216: 
217:         let project_row = |doc_row: u32| -> u16 {
218:             if doc_row < view_top {
219:                 self.area.y
220:             } else if doc_row >= view_bottom {
221:                 self.area.y + self.area.height.saturating_sub(1)
222:             } else {
223:                 self.area.y + (doc_row - view_top) as u16
224:             }
225:         };
226: 
227:         let start_row = project_row(start.row);
228:         let start_col = if start.row < view_top {
229:             self.area.x
230:         } else {
231:             start.col
232:         };
233:         let end_row = project_row(end.row);
234:         let end_col = if end.row >= view_bottom {
235:             self.area.x + self.area.width.saturating_sub(1)
236:         } else {
237:             end.col
238:         };
239: 
240:         Some(ScreenSelection {
241:             start_row,
242:             start_col,
243:             end_row,
244:             end_col,
245:         })
246:     }
247: }

253:     pub end_row: u16,

297: #[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
298: pub enum LineBreaks {
299:     #[default]
300:     EveryRow,
301:     Bitmap {
302:         line_starts: Vec<u64>,
303:         word_wraps: Vec<u64>,
304:     },
305: }
306: 
307: fn set_bit(bits: &mut Vec<u64>, row: u16) {
308:     let idx = (row / 64) as usize;
309:     if idx >= bits.len() {
310:         bits.resize(idx + 1, 0u64);
311:     }
312:     bits[idx] |= 1 << (row % 64);
313: }
314: 
315: fn get_bit(bits: &[u64], row: u16) -> bool {
316:     bits.get((row / 64) as usize)
317:         .is_some_and(|word| word & (1 << (row % 64)) != 0)
318: }
319: 
320: impl LineBreaks {
321:     pub fn from_heights(heights: impl Iterator<Item = u16>) -> Self {
322:         let mut line_starts = Vec::new();
323:         let mut row: u16 = 0;
324:         for h in heights {
325:             if h == 0 {
326:                 continue;
327:             }
328:             set_bit(&mut line_starts, row);
329:             row = row.saturating_add(h);
330:         }
331:         Self::Bitmap {
332:             line_starts,
333:             word_wraps: Vec::new(),
334:         }
335:     }
336: 
337:     pub fn from_lines(lines: &[Line<'_>], width: u16) -> Self {
338:         if width == 0 {
339:             return Self::EveryRow;
340:         }
341:         let mut line_starts = Vec::new();
342:         let mut word_wraps = Vec::new();
343:         let mut row: u16 = 0;
344:         for line in lines {
345:             if is_code_wrap_continuation(line) {
346:                 row += 1;
347:                 continue;
348:             }
349:             set_bit(&mut line_starts, row);
350:             let wrap_types = compute_wrap_types(line, width);
351:             for is_word_wrap in &wrap_types {
352:                 row += 1;
353:                 if *is_word_wrap {
354:                     set_bit(&mut word_wraps, row);
355:                 }
356:             }
357:             row += 1;
358:         }
359:         Self::Bitmap {
360:             line_starts,
361:             word_wraps,
362:         }
363:     }
364: 
365:     pub fn is_line_start(&self, row: u16) -> bool {
366:         match self {
367:             Self::EveryRow => true,
368:             Self::Bitmap { line_starts, .. } => get_bit(line_starts, row),
369:         }
370:     }
371: 
372:     pub fn needs_space(&self, row: u16) -> bool {
373:         match self {
374:             Self::EveryRow => false,
375:             Self::Bitmap { word_wraps, .. } => get_bit(word_wraps, row),
376:         }
377:     }
378: }
379: 
380: fn compute_wrap_types(line: &Line<'_>, width: u16) -> Vec<bool> {
381:     let w = width as usize;
382:     let text: String = line.spans.iter().map(|s| s.content.as_ref()).collect();
383:     let chars: Vec<char> = text.chars().collect();
384:     let mut wraps = Vec::new();
385:     let mut i = 0;
386:     let mut col = 0;
387:     let mut last_breakable: Option<usize> = None;
388: 
389:     while i < chars.len() {
390:         let ch = chars[i];
391:         let cw = ch.width().unwrap_or(0);
392: 
393:         if ch == ' ' || ch == '\t' {
394:             last_breakable = Some(i);
395:         }
396: 
397:         if col + cw > w && col > 0 {
398:             if let Some(bp) = last_breakable {
399:                 wraps.push(true);
400:                 i = bp + 1;
401:                 while i < chars.len() && chars[i] == ' ' {
402:                     i += 1;
403:                 }
404:             } else {
405:                 wraps.push(false);
406:             }
407:             col = 0;
408:             last_breakable = None;
409:             continue;
410:         }
411: 
412:         col += cw;
413:         i += 1;
414:     }
415:     wraps
416: }
417: 
418: fn is_code_wrap_continuation(line: &Line<'_>) -> bool {
419:     line.spans
420:         .first()
421:         .is_some_and(|s| s.content.as_ref() == CODE_BAR_WRAP)
422: }

427: pub struct ContentRegion<'a> {

433: pub fn inset_border(area: Rect) -> Rect {
434:     Rect::new(

437:         area.width.saturating_sub(2),
438:         area.height.saturating_sub(2),

442: pub(crate) fn range_covers(
443:     sel_start: DocPos,
444:     sel_end: DocPos,
445:     rect_top: u32,
446:     rect_bottom_incl: u32,
447:     rect_left: u16,
448:     rect_right_incl: u16,
449: ) -> bool {
450:     rect_top >= sel_start.row
451:         && rect_bottom_incl <= sel_end.row
452:         && (rect_top != sel_start.row || sel_start.col <= rect_left)
453:         && (rect_bottom_incl != sel_end.row || sel_end.col >= rect_right_incl)
454: }

456: impl ScreenSelection {

461:         range_covers(
462:             DocPos::new(self.start_row as u32, self.start_col),
463:             DocPos::new(self.end_row as u32, self.end_col),
464:             area.y as u32,
465:             area.bottom().saturating_sub(1) as u32,
466:             area.x,
467:             area.x + area.width.saturating_sub(1),
468:         )

475:         ss.start_col.max(left)
476:     } else {
477:         left
478:     };
479:     let col_end = if row == ss.end_row {
480:         ss.end_col.min(right)

482:         right

487: /// Last column is the scrollbar, so we skip it.
488: pub fn apply_highlight(buf: &mut Buffer, area: Rect, ss: &ScreenSelection) {
489:     if area.width == 0 || area.height == 0 {
490:         return;
491:     }
492:     let row_start = ss.start_row.max(area.y);
493:     let row_end = ss.end_row.min(area.bottom().saturating_sub(1));
494:     let right = area.x + area.width.saturating_sub(1);
495:     for row in row_start..=row_end {
496:         let (col_start, col_end) = col_range(ss, area.x, right, row);
497:         for col in col_start..=col_end {
498:             if col >= buf.area().right() || row >= buf.area().bottom() {
499:                 continue;
500:             }
501:             let cell = &mut buf[(col, row)];
502:             cell.set_style(cell.style().add_modifier(Modifier::REVERSED));
503:         }
504:     }
505: }
506: 
507: pub(crate) fn strip_code_bar_prefix(
508:     cell: &ratatui::buffer::Cell,
509:     out: &mut String,
510:     line_start: usize,
511: ) -> usize {
512:     if cell.style().fg != theme::current().code_gutter.fg || cell.symbol() != "│" {
513:         return 0;
514:     }
515:     let line = &out[line_start..];
516:     let prefix_len = if line.starts_with(CODE_BAR) {
517:         CODE_BAR.len()
518:     } else if line.starts_with(CODE_BAR_WRAP) {
519:         CODE_BAR_WRAP.len()
520:     } else {
521:         return 0;
522:     };
523:     out.drain(line_start..line_start + prefix_len);
524:     prefix_len
525: }
526: 
527: /// Trailing whitespace is trimmed per line. Consecutive blank lines are
528: /// collapsed so we don't emit a wall of empty newlines.
529: pub(crate) fn append_rows(
530:     buf: &Buffer,
531:     area: Rect,
532:     ss: &ScreenSelection,
533:     from: u16,
534:     to: u16,
535:     out: &mut String,
536:     breaks: &LineBreaks,
537: ) {
538:     if area.width == 0 || area.height == 0 {
539:         return;
540:     }
541:     let right = area.x + area.width.saturating_sub(1);
542:     let row_start = from.max(area.y);
543:     let row_end = to.min(area.bottom());
544:     let mut pending_newlines = 0u16;
545:     let anchor = out.len();
546:     for row in row_start..row_end {
547:         let rel_row = row - area.y;
548:         let is_new_line = breaks.is_line_start(rel_row);
549: 
550:         let (col_start, col_end) = col_range(ss, area.x, right, row);
551:         let line_start = out.len();
552:         // Wide chars (CJK, emoji) leave continuation cells with " "; skip them.
553:         let mut skip_next: usize = if col_start > area.x {
554:             UnicodeWidthStr::width(buf[(col_start - 1, row)].symbol()).saturating_sub(1)
555:         } else {
556:             0
557:         };
558:         for col in col_start..=col_end {
559:             if skip_next > 0 {
560:                 skip_next -= 1;
561:                 continue;
562:             }
563:             let sym = buf[(col, row)].symbol();
564:             let w = UnicodeWidthStr::width(sym);
565:             out.push_str(sym);
566:             skip_next = w.saturating_sub(1);
567:         }
568: 
569:         let stripped = if col_start == area.x {
570:             strip_code_bar_prefix(&buf[(col_start, row)], out, line_start)
571:         } else {
572:             0
573:         };
574: 
575:         let trimmed_len = out[line_start..].trim_end().len() + line_start;
576:         out.truncate(trimmed_len);
577:         let has_content = out.len() > line_start;
578:         let is_first_row = line_start == anchor;
579: 
580:         if is_new_line {
581:             if !has_content && !is_first_row {
582:                 pending_newlines += 1;
583:             } else if !is_first_row {
584:                 for _ in 0..pending_newlines {
585:                     out.insert(line_start, '\n');
586:                 }
587:                 pending_newlines = 0;
588:                 out.insert(line_start, '\n');
589:             }
590:         } else if has_content && !is_first_row && stripped == 0 && breaks.needs_space(rel_row) {
591:             out.insert(line_start, ' ');
592:         }
593:     }
594: }
595: 
596: /// Searched in reverse so overlays win over what is behind them.
597: pub fn extract_selected_text(
598:     buf: &Buffer,
599:     ss: &ScreenSelection,
600:     regions: &[ContentRegion<'_>],
601: ) -> String {
602:     let mut out = String::new();
603:     let mut row = ss.start_row;
604: 
605:     while row <= ss.end_row {
606:         let region = regions
607:             .iter()
608:             .rev()
609:             .find(|r| r.area.y <= row && row < r.area.bottom());
610: 
611:         let Some(region) = region else {
612:             row += 1;
613:             continue;
614:         };
615: 
616:         let region_end = region.area.bottom();
617:         let fully_selected = ss.covers_rect(region.area);
618: 
619:         if !out.is_empty() {
620:             out.push('\n');
621:         }
622:         if fully_selected && !region.raw_text.is_empty() {
623:             out.push_str(region.raw_text);
624:         } else {
625:             let chunk_end = region_end.min(ss.end_row + 1);
626:             append_rows(
627:                 buf,
628:                 region.area,
629:                 ss,
630:                 row,
631:                 chunk_end,
632:                 &mut out,
633:                 &region.line_breaks,
634:             );
635:         }
636:         row = region_end;
637:     }
638:     out
639: }

10: pub const TRUNCATION_PREFIX: &str = "...";

12: 
13: /// Add `over`'s modifiers on top of `base`, keeping `base`'s colors.
14: fn apply_modifiers(base: Style, over: Style) -> Style {
15:     base.add_modifier(over.add_modifier)
16:         .remove_modifier(over.sub_modifier)
17: }
18: 
19: /// Recolor `base` with `over`'s colors and OR the modifiers.
20: fn overlay_style(base: Style, over: Style) -> Style {
21:     let mut out = base;
22:     if let Some(fg) = over.fg {
23:         out.fg = Some(fg);
24:     }
25:     if let Some(bg) = over.bg {
26:         out.bg = Some(bg);
27:     }
28:     apply_modifiers(out, over)
29: }
30: 
31: /// When `preserve_base_color` is set (headings), emphasis only adds modifiers
32: /// so the heading colour survives. Otherwise it recolors from the theme.
33: fn apply_emphasis(base: Style, emphasis: Emphasis, preserve_base_color: bool, t: &Theme) -> Style {
34:     let emph_style = match (emphasis.bold, emphasis.italic) {
35:         (true, true) => Some(t.bold_italic),
36:         (true, false) => Some(t.bold),
37:         (false, true) => Some(t.italic),
38:         (false, false) => None,
39:     };
40:     let combine = |s: Style, over: Style| {
41:         if preserve_base_color {
42:             apply_modifiers(s, over)
43:         } else {
44:             overlay_style(s, over)
45:         }
46:     };
47:     let mut style = base;
48:     if let Some(es) = emph_style {
49:         style = combine(style, es);
50:     }
51:     if emphasis.strike {
52:         style = combine(style, t.strikethrough);
53:     }
54:     style
55: }
56: 
57: fn style_for_token(
58:     token: &StyleToken,
59:     emphasis: Emphasis,
60:     base: Style,
61:     preserve_base_color: bool,
62:     t: &Theme,
63: ) -> Style {
64:     match token {
65:         StyleToken::Text => apply_emphasis(base, emphasis, preserve_base_color, t),
66:         StyleToken::InlineCode => {
67:             let style = apply_emphasis(base, emphasis, preserve_base_color, t);
68:             overlay_style(style, t.inline_code)
69:         }
70:         StyleToken::Heading => apply_emphasis(t.heading, emphasis, true, t),
71:         StyleToken::Highlight {
72:             fg,
73:             bold,
74:             italic,
75:             underline,
76:         } => {
77:             let mut s = Style::default().fg(ratatui::style::Color::Rgb(fg.0, fg.1, fg.2));
78:             if *bold {
79:                 s = s.add_modifier(Modifier::BOLD);
80:             }
81:             if *italic {
82:                 s = s.add_modifier(Modifier::ITALIC);
83:             }
84:             if *underline {
85:                 s = s.add_modifier(Modifier::UNDERLINED);
86:             }
87:             s
88:         }
89:         StyleToken::CodeBar => t.code_gutter,
90:         StyleToken::ListMarker => t.list_marker,
91:         StyleToken::TableBorder => t.table_border,
92:         StyleToken::HorizontalRule => t.horizontal_rule,
93:     }
94: }

96: /// Heading lines preserve heading colour through emphasis. Code lines start
97: /// from `Style::default()` so highlighter colours stand alone.
98: fn paint_line(line: &RLine, text_style: Style, t: &Theme) -> Line<'static> {
99:     let (base, preserve_color) = match line.kind {
100:         LineKind::Heading => (t.heading, true),
101:         LineKind::Code => (Style::default(), false),
102:         _ => (text_style, false),
103:     };
104:     let spans = line
105:         .spans
106:         .iter()
107:         .map(
108:             |RSpan {
109:                  text,
110:                  style,
111:                  emphasis,
112:              }| {
113:                 Span::styled(
114:                     text.clone(),
115:                     style_for_token(style, *emphasis, base, preserve_color, t),
116:                 )
117:             },
118:         )
119:         .collect::<Vec<_>>();
120:     Line::from(spans)
121: }

123: pub fn should_truncate(hidden: usize) -> bool {

125: }

140: pub(crate) fn hr_line(width: u16, style: Style) -> Line<'static> {

142: }
143: 
144: fn prefix_span(prefix: &str, style: Style) -> Span<'static> {
145:     Span::styled(prefix.to_owned(), style.add_modifier(Modifier::BOLD))
146: }
147: 
148: /// Returns `Line::default()` when the prefix is empty so callers can use it
149: /// as a blank first line without an empty styled span sneaking in.
150: fn prefix_line(prefix: &str, style: Style) -> Line<'static> {
151:     if prefix.is_empty() {
152:         Line::default()
153:     } else {
154:         Line::from(prefix_span(prefix, style))
155:     }
156: }

158: /// Inline block kinds (paragraph, heading, list) share line 1 with their
159: /// prefix. Standalone kinds (code, table, hr) need a separate leader line.
160: fn shares_line_with_prefix(kind: &LineKind) -> bool {
161:     matches!(
162:         kind,
163:         LineKind::Paragraph | LineKind::Heading | LineKind::ListItem | LineKind::Blank
164:     )
165: }
166: 
167: pub fn plain_lines(
168:     text: &str,
169:     prefix: &str,
170:     text_style: Style,
171:     prefix_style: Style,
172: ) -> Vec<Line<'static>> {
173:     let text = text.trim_start_matches('\n');
174:     let mut lines: Vec<Line<'static>> = Vec::new();
175:     let mut first_line = true;
176: 
177:     for line in text.split('\n') {
178:         let mut spans: Vec<Span<'static>> = Vec::new();
179:         if first_line {
180:             if !prefix.is_empty() {
181:                 spans.push(prefix_span(prefix, prefix_style));
182:             }
183:             first_line = false;
184:         }
185:         spans.push(Span::styled(line.to_owned(), text_style));
186:         lines.push(Line::from(spans));
187:     }
188: 
189:     if lines.is_empty() {
190:         lines.push(prefix_line(prefix, prefix_style));
191:     }
192: 
193:     lines
194: }
195: 
196: /// Paint semantic lines into ratatui lines, splicing the prefix onto
197: /// the first line (or as a standalone leader for non-inline blocks).
198: pub(crate) fn paint_semantic(
199:     semantic: &[RLine],
200:     prefix: &str,
201:     text_style: Style,
202:     prefix_style: Style,
203: ) -> Vec<Line<'static>> {
204:     let t = theme::current();
205:     let mut lines: Vec<Line<'static>> = semantic
206:         .iter()
207:         .map(|l| paint_line(l, text_style, &t))
208:         .collect();
209: 
210:     if lines.is_empty() {
211:         lines.push(prefix_line(prefix, prefix_style));
212:         return lines;
213:     }
214: 
215:     if shares_line_with_prefix(&semantic[0].kind) {
216:         if !prefix.is_empty() {
217:             lines[0].spans.insert(0, prefix_span(prefix, prefix_style));
218:         }
219:     } else if !prefix.is_empty() {
220:         lines.insert(0, prefix_line(prefix, prefix_style));
221:     }
222: 
223:     lines
224: }

231:     width: u16,
232:     max_line_bytes: Option<usize>,
233: ) -> Vec<Line<'static>> {
234:     let truncated;
235:     let text = match max_line_bytes {
236:         Some(limit) => {
237:             truncated = render::truncate_long_lines_at(text, limit);
238:             truncated.as_ref()
239:         }
240:         None => text,
241:     };
242:     let semantic = render::Renderer::unwrapped().render(text, width, 0);
243:     paint_semantic(&semantic, prefix, text_style, prefix_style)
244: }
245: 
246: pub struct TruncatedOutput<'a> {
247:     pub kept: Cow<'a, str>,
248:     pub skipped: usize,
249: }
250: 
251: pub fn truncate_output(text: &str, max: usize) -> TruncatedOutput<'_> {
252:     let tr = truncate_lines(text, max);
253:     TruncatedOutput {
254:         kept: render::truncate_long_lines(tr.kept),
255:         skipped: tr.skipped,
256:     }
257: }
258: 
259: /// Keeps the head. Tools that want tail truncation do it in Lua instead
260: /// (ToolView `keep = "tail"`).
261: pub fn truncate_lines(s: &str, max: usize) -> Truncated<'_> {
262:     let Some((i, _)) = s.match_indices('\n').nth(max.saturating_sub(1)) else {
263:         return Truncated {
264:             kept: s,
265:             skipped: 0,
266:         };
267:     };
268:     let tail = &s[i..];
269:     let newlines = tail.matches('\n').count();
270:     let has_content = tail.bytes().any(|b| b != b'\n');
271:     let result = Truncated {
272:         kept: &s[..i],
273:         skipped: if has_content { newlines } else { 0 },
274:     };
275:     if result.skipped > 0 && !should_truncate(result.skipped) {
276:         return Truncated {
277:             kept: s,
278:             skipped: 0,
279:         };
280:     }
281:     result
282: }

70: pub struct ColorTransition {
71:     from: (u8, u8, u8),
72:     to: (u8, u8, u8),
73:     start: Instant,
74: }
75: 
76: impl ColorTransition {
77:     pub fn new(color: Color) -> Self {
78:         let rgb = extract_rgb(color, (100, 140, 255));
79:         Self {
80:             from: rgb,
81:             to: rgb,
82:             start: Instant::now() - std::time::Duration::from_secs_f32(COLOR_TRANSITION_SECS),
83:         }
84:     }
85: 
86:     pub fn set(&mut self, color: Color) {
87:         let rgb = extract_rgb(color, (100, 140, 255));
88:         if rgb == self.to {
89:             return;
90:         }
91:         let now = Instant::now();
92:         self.from = self.resolve_rgb(now);
93:         self.to = rgb;
94:         self.start = now;
95:     }
96: 
97:     pub fn is_animating(&self) -> bool {
98:         Instant::now().duration_since(self.start).as_secs_f32() < COLOR_TRANSITION_SECS
99:     }
100: 
101:     pub fn resolve(&self) -> Color {
102:         let (r, g, b) = self.resolve_rgb(Instant::now());
103:         Color::Rgb(r, g, b)
104:     }
105: 
106:     fn resolve_rgb(&self, now: Instant) -> (u8, u8, u8) {
107:         let t = (now.duration_since(self.start).as_secs_f32() / COLOR_TRANSITION_SECS).min(1.0);
108:         let p = ease_out_cubic(t);
109:         (
110:             lerp_u8(self.from.0, self.to.0, p),
111:             lerp_u8(self.from.1, self.to.1, p),
112:             lerp_u8(self.from.2, self.to.2, p),
113:         )
114:     }
115: }

117: pub struct Splash {

119:     field_offset: f32,
120:     animate: bool,
121:     tip_idx: usize,
122: }
123: 
124: impl Default for Splash {
125:     fn default() -> Self {
126:         Self::new(true)
127:     }
128: }
129: 
130: impl Splash {
131:     pub fn new(animate: bool) -> Self {
132:         let mut rng = [0u8; 8];
133:         getrandom::fill(&mut rng).ok();
134:         let tip_idx = u32::from_le_bytes([rng[4], rng[5], rng[6], rng[7]]) as usize % TIPS.len();
135:         Self {
136:             start: Instant::now(),
137:             field_offset: (u64::from_le_bytes(rng) % 10_000) as f32,
138:             animate,
139:             tip_idx,
140:         }
141:     }
142: 
143:     pub fn render(&self, area: Rect, buf: &mut Buffer, accent: Color) {
144:         if area.width < 20 || area.height < 5 {
145:             return;
146:         }
147: 
148:         let t = self.start.elapsed().as_secs_f32();
149:         let fade = if t >= FADE_DURATION {
150:             1.0
151:         } else {
152:             ease_out_cubic(t / FADE_DURATION)
153:         };
154: 
155:         let new_version = update::latest_version();
156:         let block_height = 8;
157:         let top_y = area.y + area.height.saturating_sub(block_height) / 2;
158:         let tag_y = top_y + 1;
159:         let help_y = tag_y + 2;
160:         let tip_y = help_y + 2;
161: 
162:         if self.animate {
163:             self.render_field(area, buf, t + self.field_offset, fade, accent);
164:         }
165:         self.render_logo(area, buf, t, fade, top_y, accent);
166:         render_centered_faded(area, buf, fade, 0.75, tag_y, TAGLINE);
167:         self.render_help(area, buf, fade, help_y, accent);
168:         self.render_tip(area, buf, fade, tip_y, accent);
169:         render_version(area, buf, fade, area.y, new_version);
170:     }
171: 
172:     fn render_field(&self, area: Rect, buf: &mut Buffer, t: f32, fade: f32, accent: Color) {
173:         let theme = theme::current();
174:         let (ac_r, ac_g, ac_b) = extract_rgb(accent, (100, 140, 255));
175:         let (bg_r, bg_g, bg_b) = extract_rgb(theme.background, (15, 15, 25));
176: 
177:         let w = area.width as usize;
178:         let h = area.height as usize;
179:         if w == 0 || h == 0 {
180:             return;
181:         }
182:         let inv_w = 1.0 / w as f32;
183:         let inv_h = 1.0 / h as f32;
184: 
185:         let layers: [(f32, f32, f32, f32); WAVE_LAYERS] = std::array::from_fn(|i| {
186:             let lf = i as f32;
187:             (
188:                 2.0 + lf * 1.8,
189:                 1.5 + lf * 1.2,
190:                 t * (0.3 + lf * 0.15) + lf * 2.094,
191:                 1.0 / (1.5 + lf * 0.5),
192:             )
193:         });
194: 
195:         let weight_sum: f32 = layers.iter().map(|l| l.3).sum();
196:         let half_weight_sum = weight_sum * 0.5;
197:         let val_scale = (fade * INTENSITY_SCALE) / half_weight_sum;
198: 
199:         let style_lut: [(&str, Style); 4] = std::array::from_fn(|i| {
200:             let idx = i + 1;
201:             let frac = idx as f32 / FIELD_CHAR_MAX;
202:             let t = FIELD_BASE_OPACITY + frac * (1.0 - FIELD_BASE_OPACITY);
203:             (
204:                 FIELD_SYMS[idx],
205:                 Style::new().fg(Color::Rgb(
206:                     lerp_u8(bg_r, ac_r, t * 0.25),
207:                     lerp_u8(bg_g, ac_g, t * 0.175),
208:                     lerp_u8(bg_b, ac_b, t * 0.325),
209:                 )),
210:             )
211:         });
212: 
213:         let vignette_inv = 1.0 / VIGNETTE_SCALE;
214: 
215:         // Single allocation for all per-column data: vx | sin0 | cos0 | sin1 | cos1 | sin2 | cos2
216:         // Contiguous SoA layout enables LLVM auto-vectorization of the inner wave loops.
217:         let mut col_data = vec![0.0_f32; w * (1 + WAVE_LAYERS * 2)];
218:         for col in 0..w {
219:             let nx = col as f32 * inv_w;
220:             let d = (nx - 0.5) * 2.0;
221:             col_data[col] = d * d;
222:             for i in 0..WAVE_LAYERS {
223:                 let (s, c) = fast_sincos(nx * layers[i].0);
224:                 col_data[w + i * 2 * w + col] = s * layers[i].3;
225:                 col_data[w + (i * 2 + 1) * w + col] = c * layers[i].3;
226:             }
227:         }
228:         let vx = &col_data[..w];
229:         let col_sin: [&[f32]; WAVE_LAYERS] =
230:             std::array::from_fn(|i| &col_data[w + i * 2 * w..w + i * 2 * w + w]);
231:         let col_cos: [&[f32]; WAVE_LAYERS] =
232:             std::array::from_fn(|i| &col_data[w + (i * 2 + 1) * w..w + (i * 2 + 2) * w]);
233: 
234:         let col_start = vx.partition_point(|&v| v > vignette_inv);
235:         let col_end = w - vx
236:             .iter()
237:             .rev()
238:             .position(|&v| v <= vignette_inv)
239:             .unwrap_or(0);
240:         if col_start >= col_end {
241:             return;
242:         }
243: 
244:         let buf_width = buf.area().width as usize;
245:         let content = &mut buf.content;
246: 
247:         let mut vals = vec![0.0_f32; col_end - col_start];
248: 
249:         for row in 0..h {
250:             let ny = row as f32 * inv_h;
251:             let d = (ny - 0.5) * 2.0;
252:             let vy = d * d;
253: 
254:             let max_vx = vignette_inv - vy;
255:             if max_vx <= 0.0 {
256:                 continue;
257:             }
258: 
259:             let row_sincos: [(f32, f32); WAVE_LAYERS] =
260:                 std::array::from_fn(|i| fast_sincos(ny * layers[i].1 + layers[i].2));
261: 
262:             let rc_start = col_start + vx[col_start..col_end].partition_point(|&v| v > max_vx);
263:             let rc_end = col_end
264:                 - vx[col_start..col_end]
265:                     .iter()
266:                     .rev()
267:                     .position(|&v| v <= max_vx)
268:                     .unwrap_or(0);
269: 
270:             let out = &mut vals[rc_start - col_start..rc_end - col_start];
271:             let vx_slice = &vx[rc_start..rc_end];
272: 
273:             // AUTOVECTORIZED - LLVM emits AVX (ymm, 8×f32) for these loops.
274:             // Do NOT add branches, function calls, or non-contiguous indexing here.
275:             // Verified via `perf annotate`.
276:             for i in 0..WAVE_LAYERS {
277:                 let (sr, cr) = row_sincos[i];
278:                 let cs = &col_sin[i][rc_start..rc_end];
279:                 let cc = &col_cos[i][rc_start..rc_end];
280:                 for j in 0..out.len() {
281:                     out[j] += cs[j] * cr + cc[j] * sr;
282:                 }
283:             }
284:             for j in 0..out.len() {
285:                 let vignette = 1.0 - (vx_slice[j] + vy) * VIGNETTE_SCALE;
286:                 out[j] = (out[j] + half_weight_sum) * vignette * val_scale;
287:             }
288: 
289:             let y = area.y + row as u16;
290:             let row_offset = y as usize * buf_width + area.x as usize;
291: 
292:             for (j, val) in out.iter_mut().enumerate() {
293:                 let idx = (*val * FIELD_CHAR_MAX + 0.5) as usize;
294:                 *val = 0.0;
295:                 if idx == 0 {
296:                     continue;
297:                 }
298:                 let (sym, style) = &style_lut[idx.min(FIELD_SYMS.len() - 1) - 1];
299: 
300:                 if let Some(cell) = content.get_mut(row_offset + rc_start + j) {
301:                     cell.set_symbol(sym).set_style(*style);
302:                 }
303:             }
304:         }
305:     }

347:

401: fn render_version(area: Rect, buf: &mut Buffer, fade: f32, y: u16, new_version: Option<&str>) {

444: fn extract_rgb(color: Color, fallback: (u8, u8, u8)) -> (u8, u8, u8) {
445:     match color {
446:         Color::Rgb(r, g, b) => (r, g, b),
447:         _ => fallback,
448:     }
449: }
450: 
451: fn faded_style(bg: (u8, u8, u8), fg: (u8, u8, u8), alpha: f32, bg_color: Color) -> Style {
452:     Style::new()
453:         .fg(Color::Rgb(
454:             lerp_u8(bg.0, fg.0, alpha),
455:             lerp_u8(bg.1, fg.1, alpha),
456:             lerp_u8(bg.2, fg.2, alpha),
457:         ))
458:         .bg(bg_color)
459: }
460: 
461: fn render_segments(area: Rect, buf: &mut Buffer, y: u16, x_start: u16, segments: &[(&str, Style)]) {
462:     let x_end = area.x + area.width;
463:     let mut x = x_start;
464:     for &(text, style) in segments {
465:         for ch in text.chars() {
466:             if x >= x_end {
467:                 return;
468:             }
469:             if let Some(cell) = buf.cell_mut((x, y)) {
470:                 cell.set_char(ch).set_style(style);
471:             }
472:             x += 1;
473:         }
474:     }
475: }
476: 
477: fn ease_out_cubic(t: f32) -> f32 {
478:     let t = t.clamp(0.0, 1.0);
479:     1.0 - (1.0 - t).powi(3)
480: }

41:     fn wrap_for_mux(&self, sequence: String) -> String {

44:             Self::Tmux => {
45:                 let escaped = sequence.replace('\u{1b}', "\u{1b}\u{1b}");

134:     let editor = std::env::var("VISUAL")
135:         .or_else(|_| std::env::var("EDITOR"))
136:         .map_err(|_| "Set $VISUAL or $EDITOR to open files".to_string())?;
137:

142:     }

144:     teardown();

147:         .args(&args[1..])
148:         .arg(path)
149:         .stdin(std::process::Stdio::inherit())
150:         .stdout(std::process::Stdio::inherit())
151:         .stderr(std::process::Stdio::inherit())
152:         .status();
153: 
154:     resume(terminal);
155: 
156:     match result {
157:         Ok(status) => Ok(status.code().unwrap_or(-1)),
158:         Err(e) => Err(format!(
159:             "Failed to open {editor}: {e} - set $VISUAL or $EDITOR"
160:         )),

165:     let mut sequence = String::new();
166:     CopyToClipboard::to_clipboard_from(text)
167:         .write_ansi(&mut sequence)
168:         .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
169:     let sequence = TerminalMux::detect().wrap_for_mux(sequence);
170:     let mut stdout = stdout().lock();
171:     stdout
172:         .write_all(sequence.as_bytes())
173:         .and_then(|()| stdout.flush())
174:         .map_err(|e| e.to_string())
175: }

180: 
181:     // Simulates DCS-passthrough parsing: `ESC ESC` becomes one ESC,
182:     // `ESC \` ends the DCS. Panics on bad input so tests fail loudly.
183:     fn parse_dcs_passthrough(wrapped: &str, prefix: &str) -> String {
184:         let body = wrapped
185:             .strip_prefix(prefix)
186:             .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("missing DCS prefix {prefix:?} in {wrapped:?}"));
187:         let bytes = body.as_bytes();
188:         let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(bytes.len());
189:         let mut i = 0;
190:         loop {
191:             match bytes.get(i) {
192:                 None => panic!("DCS body missing ST terminator: {body:?}"),
193:                 Some(&0x1B) => match bytes.get(i + 1) {
194:                     Some(&0x1B) => {
195:                         out.push(0x1B);
196:                         i += 2;
197:                     }
198:                     Some(&b'\\') => {
199:                         assert_eq!(
200:                             i + 2,
201:                             bytes.len(),
202:                             "unexpected trailing bytes after DCS ST: {:?}",
203:                             &bytes[i + 2..]
204:                         );
205:                         return String::from_utf8(out).expect("utf-8 body");
206:                     }
207:                     Some(b) => panic!("unexpected byte 0x{b:02x} after ESC inside DCS"),
208:                     None => panic!("lone trailing ESC in DCS body"),
209:                 },
210:                 Some(&b) => {
211:                     out.push(b);
212:                     i += 1;
213:                 }
214:             }
215:         }
216:     }

1: //! Mouse selection + clipboard copy.
2: //!
3: //! Enabling mouse capture (for scroll) kills the terminal's native text
4: //! selection, so we reimplement it here. A few things that are easy to get
5: //! wrong:
6: //!
7: //! Positions are stored in doc space (`DocPos`), not screen space, because
8: //! screen coords go stale the moment the user scrolls.
9: //!
10: //! Copy runs inside `view()`, not on mouse-up. The terminal buffer only
11: //! holds valid cell data during rendering, so that is the only moment we
12: //! can scrape the text. Code bar prefixes (`│ `) are stripped during
13: //! scraping so you get clean source.
14: //!
15: //! While a selection is active, `has_selection` freezes auto-scroll in the
16: //! messages panel so the viewport stays put while the user drags.
17: //!
18: //! The rightmost column of each area is reserved for the scrollbar, so
19: //! `highlight_area()` / `msg_area()` are 1 column narrower than the full
20: //! area and all column math uses `width - 1`.
21: //!
22: //! When text is word-wrapped, ratatui eats the space at the break point,
23: //! so the copied text would lose that space unless we put it back. But we
24: //! should only add a space for word-boundary wraps, not mid-word ones
25: //! (where a long token just overflows the column). `LineBreaks` tracks
26: //! both line starts and wrap types: `compute_wrap_types()` walks each
27: //! line the same way ratatui does and classifies every break, then
28: //! `append_rows` calls `needs_space()` to decide.
29:

141: /// Anchor + cursor in doc space. `area` and `zone` are captured at mouse-down
142: /// so layout changes mid-drag don't break the selection.

150: 
151: fn screen_to_doc(screen_row: u16, area: Rect, scroll_offset: u32) -> u32 {
152:     let clamped = screen_row.clamp(area.y, area.y + area.height.saturating_sub(1));
153:     scroll_offset + (clamped - area.y) as u32
154: }
155: 
156: fn clamp_col(col: u16, area: Rect) -> u16 {
157:     col.clamp(area.x, area.x + area.width.saturating_sub(1))
158: }

160: impl Selection {
161:     pub fn start(row: u16, col: u16, area: Rect, zone: SelectionZone, scroll_offset: u32) -> Self {
162:         let doc_row = screen_to_doc(row, area, scroll_offset);
163:         let doc_col = clamp_col(col, area);
164:         let pos = DocPos::new(doc_row, doc_col);
165:         Self {
166:             anchor: pos,
167:             cursor: pos,
168:             area,
169:             zone,
170:         }
171:     }

173:     pub fn update(&mut self, row: u16, col: u16, scroll_offset: u32) {
174:         self.cursor = DocPos::new(
175:             screen_to_doc(row, self.area, scroll_offset),
176:             clamp_col(col, self.area),
177:         );
178:     }

187:                 self.area.x,

190:                 self.area.height,
191:             ),
192:             _ => self.area,
193:         }
194:     }

196:     pub fn normalized(&self) -> (DocPos, DocPos) {
197:         if self.anchor <= self.cursor {
198:             (self.anchor, self.cursor)
199:         } else {
200:             (self.cursor, self.anchor)
201:         }
202:     }

204:     pub fn to_screen(self, scroll_offset: u32) -> Option<ScreenSelection> {
205:         let (start, end) = self.normalized();
206:         if start == end {
207:             return None;
208:         }
209: 
210:         let view_top = scroll_offset;
211:         let view_bottom = scroll_offset + self.area.height as u32;
212: 
213:         if end.row < view_top || start.row >= view_bottom {
214:             return None;
215:         }
216: 
217:         let project_row = |doc_row: u32| -> u16 {
218:             if doc_row < view_top {
219:                 self.area.y
220:             } else if doc_row >= view_bottom {
221:                 self.area.y + self.area.height.saturating_sub(1)
222:             } else {
223:                 self.area.y + (doc_row - view_top) as u16
224:             }
225:         };
226: 
227:         let start_row = project_row(start.row);
228:         let start_col = if start.row < view_top {
229:             self.area.x
230:         } else {
231:             start.col
232:         };
233:         let end_row = project_row(end.row);
234:         let end_col = if end.row >= view_bottom {
235:             self.area.x + self.area.width.saturating_sub(1)
236:         } else {
237:             end.col
238:         };
239: 
240:         Some(ScreenSelection {
241:             start_row,
242:             start_col,
243:             end_row,
244:             end_col,
245:         })
246:     }
247: }

297: #[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
298: pub enum LineBreaks {
299:     #[default]
300:     EveryRow,
301:     Bitmap {
302:         line_starts: Vec<u64>,
303:         word_wraps: Vec<u64>,
304:     },
305: }
306: 
307: fn set_bit(bits: &mut Vec<u64>, row: u16) {
308:     let idx = (row / 64) as usize;
309:     if idx >= bits.len() {
310:         bits.resize(idx + 1, 0u64);
311:     }
312:     bits[idx] |= 1 << (row % 64);
313: }
314: 
315: fn get_bit(bits: &[u64], row: u16) -> bool {
316:     bits.get((row / 64) as usize)
317:         .is_some_and(|word| word & (1 << (row % 64)) != 0)
318: }
319: 
320: impl LineBreaks {
321:     pub fn from_heights(heights: impl Iterator<Item = u16>) -> Self {
322:         let mut line_starts = Vec::new();
323:         let mut row: u16 = 0;
324:         for h in heights {
325:             if h == 0 {
326:                 continue;
327:             }
328:             set_bit(&mut line_starts, row);
329:             row = row.saturating_add(h);
330:         }
331:         Self::Bitmap {
332:             line_starts,
333:             word_wraps: Vec::new(),
334:         }
335:     }
336: 
337:     pub fn from_lines(lines: &[Line<'_>], width: u16) -> Self {
338:         if width == 0 {
339:             return Self::EveryRow;
340:         }
341:         let mut line_starts = Vec::new();
342:         let mut word_wraps = Vec::new();
343:         let mut row: u16 = 0;
344:         for line in lines {
345:             if is_code_wrap_continuation(line) {
346:                 row += 1;
347:                 continue;
348:             }
349:             set_bit(&mut line_starts, row);
350:             let wrap_types = compute_wrap_types(line, width);
351:             for is_word_wrap in &wrap_types {
352:                 row += 1;
353:                 if *is_word_wrap {
354:                     set_bit(&mut word_wraps, row);
355:                 }
356:             }
357:             row += 1;
358:         }
359:         Self::Bitmap {
360:             line_starts,
361:             word_wraps,
362:         }
363:     }
364: 
365:     pub fn is_line_start(&self, row: u16) -> bool {
366:         match self {
367:             Self::EveryRow => true,
368:             Self::Bitmap { line_starts, .. } => get_bit(line_starts, row),
369:         }
370:     }
371: 
372:     pub fn needs_space(&self, row: u16) -> bool {
373:         match self {
374:             Self::EveryRow => false,
375:             Self::Bitmap { word_wraps, .. } => get_bit(word_wraps, row),
376:         }
377:     }
378: }
379: 
380: fn compute_wrap_types(line: &Line<'_>, width: u16) -> Vec<bool> {
381:     let w = width as usize;
382:     let text: String = line.spans.iter().map(|s| s.content.as_ref()).collect();
383:     let chars: Vec<char> = text.chars().collect();
384:     let mut wraps = Vec::new();
385:     let mut i = 0;
386:     let mut col = 0;
387:     let mut last_breakable: Option<usize> = None;
388: 
389:     while i < chars.len() {
390:         let ch = chars[i];
391:         let cw = ch.width().unwrap_or(0);
392: 
393:         if ch == ' ' || ch == '\t' {
394:             last_breakable = Some(i);
395:         }
396: 
397:         if col + cw > w && col > 0 {
398:             if let Some(bp) = last_breakable {
399:                 wraps.push(true);
400:                 i = bp + 1;
401:                 while i < chars.len() && chars[i] == ' ' {
402:                     i += 1;
403:                 }
404:             } else {
405:                 wraps.push(false);
406:             }
407:             col = 0;
408:             last_breakable = None;
409:             continue;
410:         }
411: 
412:         col += cw;
413:         i += 1;
414:     }
415:     wraps
416: }
417: 
418: fn is_code_wrap_continuation(line: &Line<'_>) -> bool {
419:     line.spans
420:         .first()
421:         .is_some_and(|s| s.content.as_ref() == CODE_BAR_WRAP)
422: }

442: pub(crate) fn range_covers(
443:     sel_start: DocPos,
444:     sel_end: DocPos,
445:     rect_top: u32,
446:     rect_bottom_incl: u32,
447:     rect_left: u16,

450:     rect_top >= sel_start.row
451:         && rect_bottom_incl <= sel_end.row
452:         && (rect_top != sel_start.row || sel_start.col <= rect_left)
453:         && (rect_bottom_incl != sel_end.row || sel_end.col >= rect_right_incl)
454: }

464:             area.y as u32,
465:             area.bottom().saturating_sub(1) as u32,
466:             area.x,
467:             area.x + area.width.saturating_sub(1),
468:         )
469:     }
470: }
471: 
472: #[inline]
473: pub(crate) fn col_range(ss: &ScreenSelection, left: u16, right: u16, row: u16) -> (u16, u16) {
474:     let col_start = if row == ss.start_row {
475:         ss.start_col.max(left)
476:     } else {
477:         left
478:     };
479:     let col_end = if row == ss.end_row {
480:         ss.end_col.min(right)
481:     } else {
482:         right
483:     };
484:     (col_start, col_end)
485: }
486: 
487: /// Last column is the scrollbar, so we skip it.
488: pub fn apply_highlight(buf: &mut Buffer, area: Rect, ss: &ScreenSelection) {
489:     if area.width == 0 || area.height == 0 {
490:         return;
491:     }
492:     let row_start = ss.start_row.max(area.y);
493:     let row_end = ss.end_row.min(area.bottom().saturating_sub(1));
494:     let right = area.x + area.width.saturating_sub(1);
495:     for row in row_start..=row_end {
496:         let (col_start, col_end) = col_range(ss, area.x, right, row);
497:         for col in col_start..=col_end {
498:             if col >= buf.area().right() || row >= buf.area().bottom() {
499:                 continue;
500:             }
501:             let cell = &mut buf[(col, row)];
502:             cell.set_style(cell.style().add_modifier(Modifier::REVERSED));
503:         }
504:     }
505: }
506: 
507: pub(crate) fn strip_code_bar_prefix(
508:     cell: &ratatui::buffer::Cell,
509:     out: &mut String,
510:     line_start: usize,
511: ) -> usize {
512:     if cell.style().fg != theme::current().code_gutter.fg || cell.symbol() != "│" {
513:         return 0;
514:     }
515:     let line = &out[line_start..];
516:     let prefix_len = if line.starts_with(CODE_BAR) {
517:         CODE_BAR.len()
518:     } else if line.starts_with(CODE_BAR_WRAP) {
519:         CODE_BAR_WRAP.len()
520:     } else {
521:         return 0;
522:     };
523:     out.drain(line_start..line_start + prefix_len);
524:     prefix_len
525: }
526: 
527: /// Trailing whitespace is trimmed per line. Consecutive blank lines are
528: /// collapsed so we don't emit a wall of empty newlines.
529: pub(crate) fn append_rows(
530:     buf: &Buffer,
531:     area: Rect,
532:     ss: &ScreenSelection,
533:     from: u16,
534:     to: u16,
535:     out: &mut String,
536:     breaks: &LineBreaks,
537: ) {
538:     if area.width == 0 || area.height == 0 {
539:         return;
540:     }
541:     let right = area.x + area.width.saturating_sub(1);
542:     let row_start = from.max(area.y);
543:     let row_end = to.min(area.bottom());
544:     let mut pending_newlines = 0u16;
545:     let anchor = out.len();
546:     for row in row_start..row_end {
547:         let rel_row = row - area.y;
548:         let is_new_line = breaks.is_line_start(rel_row);
549: 
550:         let (col_start, col_end) = col_range(ss, area.x, right, row);
551:         let line_start = out.len();
552:         // Wide chars (CJK, emoji) leave continuation cells with " "; skip them.
553:         let mut skip_next: usize = if col_start > area.x {
554:             UnicodeWidthStr::width(buf[(col_start - 1, row)].symbol()).saturating_sub(1)
555:         } else {
556:             0
557:         };
558:         for col in col_start..=col_end {
559:             if skip_next > 0 {
560:                 skip_next -= 1;
561:                 continue;
562:             }
563:             let sym = buf[(col, row)].symbol();
564:             let w = UnicodeWidthStr::width(sym);
565:             out.push_str(sym);
566:             skip_next = w.saturating_sub(1);
567:         }
568: 
569:         let stripped = if col_start == area.x {
570:             strip_code_bar_prefix(&buf[(col_start, row)], out, line_start)
571:         } else {
572:             0
573:         };
574: 
575:         let trimmed_len = out[line_start..].trim_end().len() + line_start;
576:         out.truncate(trimmed_len);
577:         let has_content = out.len() > line_start;
578:         let is_first_row = line_start == anchor;
579: 
580:         if is_new_line {
581:             if !has_content && !is_first_row {
582:                 pending_newlines += 1;
583:             } else if !is_first_row {
584:                 for _ in 0..pending_newlines {
585:                     out.insert(line_start, '\n');
586:                 }
587:                 pending_newlines = 0;
588:                 out.insert(line_start, '\n');
589:             }
590:         } else if has_content && !is_first_row && stripped == 0 && breaks.needs_space(rel_row) {
591:             out.insert(line_start, ' ');
592:         }
593:     }
594: }
595: 
596: /// Searched in reverse so overlays win over what is behind them.
597: pub fn extract_selected_text(
598:     buf: &Buffer,
599:     ss: &ScreenSelection,
600:     regions: &[ContentRegion<'_>],
601: ) -> String {
602:     let mut out = String::new();
603:     let mut row = ss.start_row;
604: 
605:     while row <= ss.end_row {
606:         let region = regions
607:             .iter()
608:             .rev()
609:             .find(|r| r.area.y <= row && row < r.area.bottom());
610: 
611:         let Some(region) = region else {
612:             row += 1;
613:             continue;
614:         };
615: 
616:         let region_end = region.area.bottom();
617:         let fully_selected = ss.covers_rect(region.area);
618: 
619:         if !out.is_empty() {
620:             out.push('\n');
621:         }
622:         if fully_selected && !region.raw_text.is_empty() {
623:             out.push_str(region.raw_text);
624:         } else {
625:             let chunk_end = region_end.min(ss.end_row + 1);
626:             append_rows(
627:                 buf,
628:                 region.area,
629:                 ss,
630:                 row,
631:                 chunk_end,
632:                 &mut out,
633:                 &region.line_breaks,
634:             );
635:         }
636:         row = region_end;
637:     }
638:     out
639: }

981:     fn range_covers_cases(
982:         sel_start: DocPos,

10: pub const TRUNCATION_PREFIX: &str = "...";
11: const MIN_TRUNCATABLE_LINES: usize = 2;
12: 
13: /// Add `over`'s modifiers on top of `base`, keeping `base`'s colors.
14: fn apply_modifiers(base: Style, over: Style) -> Style {
15:     base.add_modifier(over.add_modifier)
16:         .remove_modifier(over.sub_modifier)
17: }
18: 
19: /// Recolor `base` with `over`'s colors and OR the modifiers.
20: fn overlay_style(base: Style, over: Style) -> Style {
21:     let mut out = base;
22:     if let Some(fg) = over.fg {
23:         out.fg = Some(fg);
24:     }
25:     if let Some(bg) = over.bg {
26:         out.bg = Some(bg);
27:     }
28:     apply_modifiers(out, over)
29: }
30: 
31: /// When `preserve_base_color` is set (headings), emphasis only adds modifiers
32: /// so the heading colour survives. Otherwise it recolors from the theme.
33: fn apply_emphasis(base: Style, emphasis: Emphasis, preserve_base_color: bool, t: &Theme) -> Style {
34:     let emph_style = match (emphasis.bold, emphasis.italic) {
35:         (true, true) => Some(t.bold_italic),
36:         (true, false) => Some(t.bold),
37:         (false, true) => Some(t.italic),
38:         (false, false) => None,
39:     };
40:     let combine = |s: Style, over: Style| {
41:         if preserve_base_color {
42:             apply_modifiers(s, over)
43:         } else {
44:             overlay_style(s, over)
45:         }
46:     };
47:     let mut style = base;
48:     if let Some(es) = emph_style {
49:         style = combine(style, es);
50:     }
51:     if emphasis.strike {
52:         style = combine(style, t.strikethrough);
53:     }
54:     style
55: }
56: 
57: fn style_for_token(
58:     token: &StyleToken,
59:     emphasis: Emphasis,
60:     base: Style,
61:     preserve_base_color: bool,
62:     t: &Theme,
63: ) -> Style {
64:     match token {
65:         StyleToken::Text => apply_emphasis(base, emphasis, preserve_base_color, t),
66:         StyleToken::InlineCode => {
67:             let style = apply_emphasis(base, emphasis, preserve_base_color, t);
68:             overlay_style(style, t.inline_code)
69:         }
70:         StyleToken::Heading => apply_emphasis(t.heading, emphasis, true, t),
71:         StyleToken::Highlight {
72:             fg,
73:             bold,
74:             italic,
75:             underline,
76:         } => {
77:             let mut s = Style::default().fg(ratatui::style::Color::Rgb(fg.0, fg.1, fg.2));
78:             if *bold {
79:                 s = s.add_modifier(Modifier::BOLD);
80:             }
81:             if *italic {
82:                 s = s.add_modifier(Modifier::ITALIC);
83:             }
84:             if *underline {
85:                 s = s.add_modifier(Modifier::UNDERLINED);
86:             }
87:             s
88:         }
89:         StyleToken::CodeBar => t.code_gutter,
90:         StyleToken::ListMarker => t.list_marker,
91:         StyleToken::TableBorder => t.table_border,
92:         StyleToken::HorizontalRule => t.horizontal_rule,
93:     }
94: }
95: 
96: /// Heading lines preserve heading colour through emphasis. Code lines start
97: /// from `Style::default()` so highlighter colours stand alone.
98: fn paint_line(line: &RLine, text_style: Style, t: &Theme) -> Line<'static> {
99:     let (base, preserve_color) = match line.kind {
100:         LineKind::Heading => (t.heading, true),
101:         LineKind::Code => (Style::default(), false),
102:         _ => (text_style, false),
103:     };
104:     let spans = line
105:         .spans
106:         .iter()
107:         .map(
108:             |RSpan {
109:                  text,
110:                  style,
111:                  emphasis,
112:              }| {
113:                 Span::styled(
114:                     text.clone(),
115:                     style_for_token(style, *emphasis, base, preserve_color, t),
116:                 )
117:             },
118:         )
119:         .collect::<Vec<_>>();
120:     Line::from(spans)
121: }

146: pub(crate) fn hr_line(width: u16, style: Style) -> Line<'static> {
147:     Line::from(Span::styled(render::hr_text(width), style))
148: }
149: 
150: fn prefix_span(prefix: &str, style: Style) -> Span<'static> {
151:     Span::styled(prefix.to_owned(), style.add_modifier(Modifier::BOLD))
152: }
153: 
154: /// Returns `Line::default()` when the prefix is empty so callers can use it
155: /// as a blank first line without an empty styled span sneaking in.
156: fn prefix_line(prefix: &str, style: Style) -> Line<'static> {
157:     if prefix.is_empty() {
158:         Line::default()
159:     } else {
160:         Line::from(prefix_span(prefix, style))
161:     }
162: }
163: 
164: /// Inline block kinds (paragraph, heading, list) share line 1 with their
165: /// prefix. Standalone kinds (code, table, hr) need a separate leader line.
166: fn shares_line_with_prefix(kind: &LineKind) -> bool {
167:     matches!(
168:         kind,
169:         LineKind::Paragraph | LineKind::Heading | LineKind::ListItem | LineKind::Blank
170:     )
171: }
172: 
173: pub fn plain_lines(
174:     text: &str,
175:     prefix: &str,
176:     text_style: Style,
177:     prefix_style: Style,
178: ) -> Vec<Line<'static>> {
179:     let text = text.trim_start_matches('\n');
180:     let mut lines: Vec<Line<'static>> = Vec::new();
181:     let mut first_line = true;
182: 
183:     for line in text.split('\n') {
184:         let mut spans: Vec<Span<'static>> = Vec::new();
185:         if first_line {
186:             if !prefix.is_empty() {
187:                 spans.push(prefix_span(prefix, prefix_style));
188:             }
189:             first_line = false;
190:         }
191:         spans.push(Span::styled(line.to_owned(), text_style));
192:         lines.push(Line::from(spans));
193:     }
194: 
195:     if lines.is_empty() {
196:         lines.push(prefix_line(prefix, prefix_style));
197:     }
198: 
199:     lines
200: }

202: /// Paint semantic lines into ratatui lines, splicing the prefix onto
203: /// the first line (or as a standalone leader for non-inline blocks).
204: pub(crate) fn paint_semantic(
205:     semantic: &[RLine],
206:     prefix: &str,
207:     text_style: Style,
208:     prefix_style: Style,
209: ) -> Vec<Line<'static>> {
210:     let t = theme::current();
211:     let mut lines: Vec<Line<'static>> = semantic
212:         .iter()
213:         .map(|l| paint_line(l, text_style, &t))
214:         .collect();
215: 
216:     if lines.is_empty() {
217:         lines.push(prefix_line(prefix, prefix_style));
218:         return lines;
219:     }
220: 
221:     if shares_line_with_prefix(&semantic[0].kind) {
222:         if !prefix.is_empty() {
223:             lines[0].spans.insert(0, prefix_span(prefix, prefix_style));
224:         }
225:     } else if !prefix.is_empty() {
226:         lines.insert(0, prefix_line(prefix, prefix_style));
227:     }
228: 
229:     lines
230: }
231: 
232: pub fn text_to_lines(
233:     text: &str,
234:     prefix: &str,
235:     text_style: Style,
236:     prefix_style: Style,
237:     width: u16,
238:     max_line_bytes: Option<usize>,
239: ) -> Vec<Line<'static>> {
240:     let truncated;
241:     let text = match max_line_bytes {
242:         Some(limit) => {
243:             truncated = render::truncate_long_lines_at(text, limit);
244:             truncated.as_ref()
245:         }
246:         None => text,
247:     };
248:     let semantic = render::Renderer::unwrapped().render(text, width, 0);
249:     paint_semantic(&semantic, prefix, text_style, prefix_style)
250: }
251: 
252: pub struct TruncatedOutput<'a> {
253:     pub kept: Cow<'a, str>,
254:     pub skipped: usize,
255: }
256: 
257: pub fn truncate_output(text: &str, max: usize, keep: Keep) -> TruncatedOutput<'_> {
258:     let tr = truncate_lines(text, max, keep);
259:     TruncatedOutput {
260:         kept: render::truncate_long_lines(tr.kept),
261:         skipped: tr.skipped,
262:     }
263: }
264: 
265: pub fn truncate_lines(s: &str, max: usize, keep: Keep) -> Truncated<'_> {
266:     let split = match keep {
267:         Keep::Head => s.match_indices('\n').nth(max.saturating_sub(1)),
268:         Keep::Tail => s.rmatch_indices('\n').nth(max.saturating_sub(1)),
269:     };
270:     let Some((i, _)) = split else {
271:         return Truncated {
272:             kept: s,
273:             skipped: 0,
274:         };
275:     };
276:     let result = match keep {
277:         Keep::Head => {
278:             let tail = &s[i..];
279:             let newlines = tail.matches('\n').count();
280:             let has_content = tail.bytes().any(|b| b != b'\n');
281:             Truncated {
282:                 kept: &s[..i],
283:                 skipped: if has_content { newlines } else { 0 },
284:             }
285:         }
286:         Keep::Tail => {
287:             let head = &s[..i];
288:             let newlines = head.matches('\n').count() + 1;
289:             let has_content = head.bytes().any(|b| b != b'\n');
290:             Truncated {
291:                 kept: &s[i + 1..],
292:                 skipped: if has_content { newlines } else { 0 },
293:             }
294:         }
295:     };
296:     if result.skipped > 0 && !should_truncate(result.skipped) {
297:         return Truncated {
298:             kept: s,
299:             skipped: 0,
300:         };
301:     }
302:     result
303: }

40:     }
41: 
42:     pub fn with_speed(ms_per_char: u64) -> Self {
43:         Self {
44:             buffer: String::new(),
45:             visible_len: 0,
46:             visible_byte_offset: 0,
47:             anim_start_visible: 0,
48:             anim_target: 0,
49:             anim_start_at: Instant::now(),
50:             anim_duration: Duration::ZERO,
51:             ms_per_char,
52:         }
53:     }
54: 
55:     pub fn push(&mut self, text: &str) {
56:         self.buffer.push_str(text);
57:         self.tick();
58:         self.anim_start_visible = self.visible_len;
59:         self.anim_target = self.buffer.chars().count();
60:         if self.ms_per_char == 0 {
61:             self.advance_visible(self.anim_target);
62:             return;
63:         }
64:         let unrevealed = self.anim_target - self.anim_start_visible;
65:         let ms = (unrevealed as u64 * self.ms_per_char).clamp(MIN_DURATION_MS, MAX_DURATION_MS);
66:         self.anim_duration = Duration::from_millis(ms);
67:         self.anim_start_at = Instant::now();
68:     }
69: 
70:     pub fn tick(&mut self) {
71:         if self.visible_len >= self.anim_target {
72:             return;
73:         }
74:         let elapsed = self.anim_start_at.elapsed();
75:         let progress = (elapsed.as_secs_f64() / self.anim_duration.as_secs_f64()).min(1.0);
76:         let delta = self.anim_target - self.anim_start_visible;
77:         let new_len = self.anim_start_visible + (delta as f64 * progress).round() as usize;
78:         self.advance_visible(new_len);
79:     }
80: 
81:     pub fn visible(&self) -> &str {
82:         &self.buffer[..self.visible_byte_offset]
83:     }
84: 
85:     pub fn is_animating(&self) -> bool {
86:         self.visible_len < self.anim_target
87:     }
88: 
89:     pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
90:         self.buffer.is_empty()
91:     }
92:

94:         if self.buffer.is_empty() {
95:             0
96:         } else {
97:             self.buffer.bytes().filter(|&b| b == b'\n').count() + 1
98:         }
99:     }
100:

102:         self.buffer.clear();
103:         self.reset_anim();
104:     }

108:         mem::take(&mut self.buffer)
109:     }

113:         self.buffer = text.into();
114:         let len = self.buffer.chars().count();
115:         self.visible_len = len;
116:         self.visible_byte_offset = self.buffer.len();
117:         self.anim_start_visible = len;
118:         self.anim_target = len;
119:         self.anim_duration = Duration::ZERO;
120:     }
121: 
122:     fn reset_anim(&mut self) {
123:         self.visible_len = 0;
124:         self.visible_byte_offset = 0;
125:         self.anim_start_visible = 0;
126:         self.anim_target = 0;

129:     fn advance_visible(&mut self, new_len: usize) {
130:         let skip = new_len - self.visible_len;

133:                 .char_indices()

135:                 .map_or(self.buffer.len(), |(i, _)| self.visible_byte_offset + i);
136:         }

138:     }

48:         self.btw_modal.open(&question, rx);

63: async fn run_btw(
64:     provider: Arc<dyn Provider>,
65:     model: Model,
66:     system: String,
67:     messages: Vec<Message>,
68:     btw_tx: Sender<BtwEvent>,
69:     session_id: Option<String>,
70: ) {
71:     let (event_tx, event_rx) = flume::unbounded();
72:     let tools = Value::Array(vec![]);
73:     let messages = maki_providers::adapt_images_for_model(&model, &messages);

75:     let stream_fut = provider.stream_message(
76:         &model,
77:         &messages,
78:         &system,
79:         &tools,
80:         &event_tx,
81:         RequestOptions::default(),
82:         session_id.as_deref(),
83:     );
84: 
85:     let forward_fut = async {
86:         while let Ok(event) = event_rx.recv_async().await {
87:             let delta = match event {
88:                 ProviderEvent::TextDelta { text } | ProviderEvent::ThinkingDelta { text } => text,
89:                 _ => continue,
90:             };
91:             if btw_tx.send(BtwEvent::TextDelta(delta)).is_err() {
92:                 return;
93:             }
94:         }
95:     };

102:         }
103:         Err(e) => {

137:         self.main_chat()
138:             .show_user_message(format_with_images(text, image_count));
139:     }

168:         self.render_tip(area, buf, fade, tip_y, accent);
169:         render_version(area, buf, fade, area.y, new_version);

172:     fn render_field(&self, area: Rect, buf: &mut Buffer, t: f32, fade: f32, accent: Color) {
173:         let theme = theme::current();
174:         let (ac_r, ac_g, ac_b) = extract_rgb(accent, (100, 140, 255));
175:         let (bg_r, bg_g, bg_b) = extract_rgb(theme.background, (15, 15, 25));
176: 
177:         let w = area.width as usize;
178:         let h = area.height as usize;
179:         if w == 0 || h == 0 {
180:             return;
181:         }
182:         let inv_w = 1.0 / w as f32;
183:         let inv_h = 1.0 / h as f32;
184: 
185:         let layers: [(f32, f32, f32, f32); WAVE_LAYERS] = std::array::from_fn(|i| {
186:             let lf = i as f32;
187:             (
188:                 2.0 + lf * 1.8,
189:                 1.5 + lf * 1.2,
190:                 t * (0.3 + lf * 0.15) + lf * 2.094,
191:                 1.0 / (1.5 + lf * 0.5),
192:             )
193:         });
194: 
195:         let weight_sum: f32 = layers.iter().map(|l| l.3).sum();
196:         let half_weight_sum = weight_sum * 0.5;
197:         let val_scale = (fade * INTENSITY_SCALE) / half_weight_sum;
198: 
199:         let style_lut: [(&str, Style); 4] = std::array::from_fn(|i| {
200:             let idx = i + 1;
201:             let frac = idx as f32 / FIELD_CHAR_MAX;
202:             let t = FIELD_BASE_OPACITY + frac * (1.0 - FIELD_BASE_OPACITY);
203:             (
204:                 FIELD_SYMS[idx],
205:                 Style::new().fg(Color::Rgb(
206:                     lerp_u8(bg_r, ac_r, t * 0.25),
207:                     lerp_u8(bg_g, ac_g, t * 0.175),
208:                     lerp_u8(bg_b, ac_b, t * 0.325),
209:                 )),
210:             )
211:         });
212: 
213:         let vignette_inv = 1.0 / VIGNETTE_SCALE;
214: 
215:         // Single allocation for all per-column data: vx | sin0 | cos0 | sin1 | cos1 | sin2 | cos2
216:         // Contiguous SoA layout enables LLVM auto-vectorization of the inner wave loops.
217:         let mut col_data = vec![0.0_f32; w * (1 + WAVE_LAYERS * 2)];
218:         for col in 0..w {
219:             let nx = col as f32 * inv_w;
220:             let d = (nx - 0.5) * 2.0;
221:             col_data[col] = d * d;
222:             for i in 0..WAVE_LAYERS {
223:                 let (s, c) = fast_sincos(nx * layers[i].0);
224:                 col_data[w + i * 2 * w + col] = s * layers[i].3;
225:                 col_data[w + (i * 2 + 1) * w + col] = c * layers[i].3;
226:             }
227:         }
228:         let vx = &col_data[..w];
229:         let col_sin: [&[f32]; WAVE_LAYERS] =
230:             std::array::from_fn(|i| &col_data[w + i * 2 * w..w + i * 2 * w + w]);
231:         let col_cos: [&[f32]; WAVE_LAYERS] =
232:             std::array::from_fn(|i| &col_data[w + (i * 2 + 1) * w..w + (i * 2 + 2) * w]);
233: 
234:         let col_start = vx.partition_point(|&v| v > vignette_inv);
235:         let col_end = w - vx
236:             .iter()
237:             .rev()
238:             .position(|&v| v <= vignette_inv)
239:             .unwrap_or(0);
240:         if col_start >= col_end {
241:             return;
242:         }
243: 
244:         let buf_width = buf.area().width as usize;
245:         let content = &mut buf.content;

247:         let mut vals = vec![0.0_f32; col_end - col_start];

251:             let d = (ny - 0.5) * 2.0;
252:             let vy = d * d;
253: 
254:             let max_vx = vignette_inv - vy;
255:             if max_vx <= 0.0 {
256:                 continue;
257:             }
258: 
259:             let row_sincos: [(f32, f32); WAVE_LAYERS] =
260:                 std::array::from_fn(|i| fast_sincos(ny * layers[i].1 + layers[i].2));
261: 
262:             let rc_start = col_start + vx[col_start..col_end].partition_point(|&v| v > max_vx);
263:             let rc_end = col_end
264:                 - vx[col_start..col_end]
265:                     .iter()
266:                     .rev()
267:                     .position(|&v| v <= max_vx)
268:                     .unwrap_or(0);
269: 
270:             let out = &mut vals[rc_start - col_start..rc_end - col_start];
271:             let vx_slice = &vx[rc_start..rc_end];
272: 
273:             // AUTOVECTORIZED - LLVM emits AVX (ymm, 8×f32) for these loops.
274:             // Do NOT add branches, function calls, or non-contiguous indexing here.
275:             // Verified via `perf annotate`.
276:             for i in 0..WAVE_LAYERS {
277:                 let (sr, cr) = row_sincos[i];
278:                 let cs = &col_sin[i][rc_start..rc_end];
279:                 let cc = &col_cos[i][rc_start..rc_end];
280:                 for j in 0..out.len() {
281:                     out[j] += cs[j] * cr + cc[j] * sr;
282:                 }
283:             }
284:             for j in 0..out.len() {
285:                 let vignette = 1.0 - (vx_slice[j] + vy) * VIGNETTE_SCALE;
286:                 out[j] = (out[j] + half_weight_sum) * vignette * val_scale;
287:             }
288: 
289:             let y = area.y + row as u16;
290:             let row_offset = y as usize * buf_width + area.x as usize;
291: 
292:             for (j, val) in out.iter_mut().enumerate() {
293:                 let idx = (*val * FIELD_CHAR_MAX + 0.5) as usize;
294:                 *val = 0.0;
295:                 if idx == 0 {
296:                     continue;
297:                 }
298:                 let (sym, style) = &style_lut[idx.min(FIELD_SYMS.len() - 1) - 1];
299: 
300:                 if let Some(cell) = content.get_mut(row_offset + rc_start + j) {
301:                     cell.set_symbol(sym).set_style(*style);
302:                 }
303:             }
304:         }
305:     }

444: fn extract_rgb(color: Color, fallback: (u8, u8, u8)) -> (u8, u8, u8) {
445:     match color {
446:         Color::Rgb(r, g, b) => (r, g, b),
447:         _ => fallback,
448:     }
449: }
450: 
451: fn faded_style(bg: (u8, u8, u8), fg: (u8, u8, u8), alpha: f32, bg_color: Color) -> Style {
452:     Style::new()
453:         .fg(Color::Rgb(
454:             lerp_u8(bg.0, fg.0, alpha),
455:             lerp_u8(bg.1, fg.1, alpha),
456:             lerp_u8(bg.2, fg.2, alpha),
457:         ))
458:         .bg(bg_color)
459: }
460: 
461: fn render_segments(area: Rect, buf: &mut Buffer, y: u16, x_start: u16, segments: &[(&str, Style)]) {
462:     let x_end = area.x + area.width;
463:     let mut x = x_start;
464:     for &(text, style) in segments {
465:         for ch in text.chars() {
466:             if x >= x_end {
467:                 return;
468:             }
469:             if let Some(cell) = buf.cell_mut((x, y)) {
470:                 cell.set_char(ch).set_style(style);
471:             }
472:             x += 1;
473:         }
474:     }
475: }

477: fn ease_out_cubic(t: f32) -> f32 {
478:     let t = t.clamp(0.0, 1.0);
479:     1.0 - (1.0 - t).powi(3)
480: }

181:     // Simulates DCS-passthrough parsing: `ESC ESC` becomes one ESC,
182:     // `ESC \` ends the DCS. Panics on bad input so tests fail loudly.
183:     fn parse_dcs_passthrough(wrapped: &str, prefix: &str) -> String {
184:         let body = wrapped
185:             .strip_prefix(prefix)
186:             .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("missing DCS prefix {prefix:?} in {wrapped:?}"));
187:         let bytes = body.as_bytes();
188:         let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(bytes.len());
189:         let mut i = 0;
190:         loop {
191:             match bytes.get(i) {
192:                 None => panic!("DCS body missing ST terminator: {body:?}"),
193:                 Some(&0x1B) => match bytes.get(i + 1) {
194:                     Some(&0x1B) => {
195:                         out.push(0x1B);
196:                         i += 2;

206:                     }

### 5. `markdown.rs`
- **Fork**: 557 lines | **Upstream**: 585 lines
- **Status**: **Modified** — the only file with changes
- **What changed**: Upstream defines a `Keep` enum (`Head`/`Tail`) and both `truncate_lines` and `truncate_output` take `keep: Keep` as a parameter, supporting both head and tail truncation. The fork **removed** the `Keep` enum (lines 123–127 upstream) and both functions were simplified to always keep the head — the `keep` parameter was dropped.
  - `truncate_lines(s, max, keep)` → `truncate_lines(s, max)` 
  - `truncate_output(text, max, keep)` → `truncate_output(text, max)`
  - The doc comment updating was also simplified (line 260: "Tools that want tail truncation do it in Lua instead").
- **Fork-specific API deps**: `maki_markdown::{Emphasis, render::{...}}`, `ratatui`

### 6. `splash.rs` (537 lines)

- **Fork-specific API deps**: `ratatui`, `crate::theme`, `crate::update`, `crate::components::keybindings`, `getrandom`

### 7. `terminal.rs` (272 lines)

353:     pub fn update(&mut self, msg: Msg) -> Vec<Action> {
354:         match msg {
355:             Msg::Key(key) => self.handle_key(key),
356:             Msg::Paste(text) => {
357:                 let text = text.replace("\r\n", "\n").replace('\r', "\n");
358:                 if text.is_empty() {
359:                     if self.is_main_chat() && self.image_paste_rx.is_empty() {
360:                         self.start_image_paste();
361:                     }
362:                 } else {
363:                     let mut any_image = false;
364:                     if self.is_main_chat() {
365:                         for line in text.lines() {
366:                             if let Some((path, mt)) = image::try_parse_image_path(line) {
367:                                 self.start_file_image_paste(path, mt);
368:                                 any_image = true;
369:                             }
370:                         }
371:                     }
372:                     if !any_image {
373:                         self.route_text_paste(&text);
374:                     }
375:                 }
376:                 vec![]
377:             }
378:             Msg::Mouse(event) => {
379:                 self.handle_mouse(event);
380:                 vec![]
381:             }
382:             Msg::Scroll { column, row, delta } => {
383:                 self.clear_selection_unless_pending_copy();
384:                 self.handle_scroll(column, row, delta);
385:                 vec![]
386:             }
387:             Msg::Agent(envelope) => self.handle_agent_event(*envelope),
388:         }
389:     }
390: 
391:     fn send_answer(&self, answer: String) {
392:         if let Some(tx) = &self.answer_tx {
393:             let _ = tx.try_send(answer);
394:         }
395:     }
396: 
397:     fn send_to_agent(&self, subagent_id: Option<&str>, answer: String) {
398:         let routed = subagent_id.and_then(|id| self.subagent_answers.get(id));
399:         if let Some(tx) = routed {
400:             let _ = tx.try_send(answer);
401:         } else {
402:             self.send_answer(answer);
403:         }
404:     }
405: 
406:     fn handle_scroll(&mut self, column: u16, row: u16, delta: i32) {
407:         if self.btw_modal.is_open() {
408:             self.btw_modal.scroll(delta);
409:             return;
410:         }
411:         if self.help_modal.is_open() {
412:             self.help_modal.scroll(delta);
413:             return;
414:         }
415:         let pos = Position::new(column, row);
416:         if self.float_mgr.is_open() && self.float_mgr.contains(pos) {
417:             self.float_mgr.scroll(delta);
418:             return;
419:         }
420:         macro_rules! try_picker {
421:             ($picker:expr) => {
422:                 if $picker.is_open() {
423:                     if $picker.contains(pos) {
424:                         $picker.scroll(delta);
425:                     }
426:                     return;
427:                 }
428:             };
429:         }
430:         try_picker!(self.session_picker);
431:         try_picker!(self.rewind_picker);
432:         try_picker!(self.goto_picker);
433:         try_picker!(self.task_picker);
434:         try_picker!(self.model_picker);
435:         try_picker!(self.file_picker);
436:         if let Some(zone) = self.zone_at(row, column) {
437:             self.scroll_zone(zone.zone, delta);
438:         }
439:     }
440: 
441:     fn open_tasks(&mut self) {
442:         let entries: Vec<TaskEntry> = self
443:             .chats
444:             .iter()
445:             .enumerate()
446:             .map(|(i, c)| TaskEntry {
447:                 name: c.name.clone(),
448:                 finished: (i > 0).then_some(c.is_finished()),
449:             })
450:             .collect();
451:         self.task_picker_original = Some(self.active_chat);
452:         self.task_picker.open(entries, " Tasks ");
453:         self.task_picker.select(self.active_chat);
454:     }
