```
462: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
463: pub struct RequestOptions {
464:     pub thinking: ThinkingConfig,
465:     /// Raw user preference, reconciled by [`RequestOptions::clamped`] before use.
466:     pub fast: bool,
467: }
468: 
469: impl RequestOptions {
470:     /// Strips options the model does not support. Called once before every
471:     /// request so UI state, restored sessions, and subagent flags all go
472:     /// through the same gate.
473:     pub fn clamped(self, model: &crate::model::Model) -> Self {
474:         Self {
475:             thinking: if model.supports_thinking() {
476:                 self.thinking
477:             } else {
478:                 ThinkingConfig::Off
479:             },
480:             fast: self.fast && model.supports_fast(),
481:         }
482:     }
483: }

493: /// provider exposes a programmatic quota endpoint; check `Provider::fetch_usage`.
494: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
495: pub struct ProviderUsage {

497:     #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
498:     pub plan: Option<String>,

500: }

502: /// A single quota window (e.g. a 5-hour or weekly token quota).
503: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
504: pub struct UsageLimit {
505:     /// Human-readable label for the window, provided by the provider.
506:     pub label: String,
507:     /// Usage percentage within the window, 0-100.
508:     pub percentage: u32,
509:     /// When the window resets, as epoch milliseconds.
510:     #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
511:     pub reset_at: Option<u64>,
512:     /// Extra provider-supplied context, e.g. "$2.33 spent" for usage credits.
513:     #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
514:     pub detail: Option<String>,
515: }
```

```
159: pub struct ModelEntry {

171: fn lookup_entry<'a>(
172:     entries: &'a [ModelEntry],
173:     model_id: &str,
174: ) -> Result<&'a ModelEntry, ModelError> {
175:     entries
176:         .iter()
177:         .flat_map(|e| e.prefixes.iter().map(move |p| (p, e)))
178:         .filter(|(p, _)| model_id.starts_with(*p))
179:         .max_by_key(|(p, _)| p.len())
180:         .map(|(_, e)| e)
181:         .ok_or_else(|| ModelError::UnknownModel(model_id.to_string()))
182: }

184: pub fn models_for_provider(provider: ProviderKind) -> &'static [ModelEntry] {
185:     match provider {
186:         ProviderKind::Anthropic => anthropic::models(),
187:         ProviderKind::OpenAi => openai::models(),
188:         ProviderKind::Copilot => copilot::models(),
189:         ProviderKind::Ollama => ollama::models(),
190:         ProviderKind::LlamaCpp => llama_cpp::models(),
191:         ProviderKind::Mistral => mistral::models(),
192:         ProviderKind::Google => google::models(),
193:         ProviderKind::Zai => zai::models(),
194:         ProviderKind::Synthetic => synthetic::models(),
195:         ProviderKind::TensorX => tensorx::models(),
196:         ProviderKind::DeepSeek => deepseek::models(),
197:         ProviderKind::OpenRouter => openrouter::models(),
198:         ProviderKind::Opencode => &[],
199:     }
200: }

207:         }

217: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
218: pub struct Model {
219:     pub id: String,
220:     pub provider: ProviderKind,
221:     pub dynamic_slug: Option<String>,
222:     pub tier: ModelTier,
223:     pub family: ModelFamily,
224:     pub supports_tool_examples_override: Option<bool>,
225:     pub supports_thinking_override: Option<bool>,
226:     /// Resolved once at construction so every consumer reads the same answer.
227:     pub vision: bool,
228:     pub pricing: ModelPricing,
229:     pub max_output_tokens: u32,
230:     pub context_window: u32,
231: }
232: 
233: impl Model {
234:     /// When no static entry matches (a freshly released model the table has not
235:     /// caught up to yet), fall back to the provider defaults so it still resolves.
236:     fn from_base(provider: ProviderKind, model_id: &str, dynamic_slug: Option<&str>) -> Self {
237:         let static_entry = lookup_entry(models_for_provider(provider), model_id).ok();
238:         let spec = match dynamic_slug {
239:             Some(slug) => format!("{slug}/{model_id}"),
240:             None => format!("{provider}/{model_id}"),
241:         };
242:         let tier = crate::model_registry::model_registry()
243:             .read()
244:             .unwrap()
245:             .tier_for(&spec, provider, static_entry.map(|e| e.tier));
246:         let (family, pricing, max_output_tokens, context_window, vision) = match static_entry {
247:             Some(e) => (
248:                 e.family,
249:                 e.pricing.clone(),
250:                 e.max_output_tokens,
251:                 anthropic::shared::long_context_window(model_id).unwrap_or(e.context_window),
252:                 e.vision,
253:             ),
254:             None => {
255:                 let guard = crate::model_registry::model_registry().read().unwrap();
256:                 let discovered = guard.discovered(provider, model_id);
257:                 (
258:                     provider.family(),
259:                     discovered
260:                         .and_then(|d| d.pricing.clone())
261:                         .unwrap_or_default(),
262:                     discovered
263:                         .and_then(|d| d.max_output_tokens)
264:                         .unwrap_or_else(|| provider.fallback_max_output()),
265:                     discovered
266:                         .and_then(|d| d.context_window)
267:                         .unwrap_or_else(|| provider.fallback_context_window()),
268:                     provider.family().supports_vision(),
269:                 )
270:             }
271:         };
272:         Self {
273:             id: model_id.to_string(),
274:             provider,
275:             dynamic_slug: dynamic_slug.map(str::to_string),
276:             tier,
277:             family,
278:             supports_tool_examples_override: None,
279:             supports_thinking_override: None,
280:             vision,
281:             pricing,
282:             max_output_tokens,
283:             context_window,
284:         }
285:     }
286: 
287:     pub fn supports_thinking(&self) -> bool {
288:         self.supports_thinking_override
289:             .or_else(|| {
290:                 let guard = crate::model_registry::model_registry().read().unwrap();
291:                 guard
292:                     .discovered(self.provider, &self.id)
293:                     .and_then(|d| d.supports_thinking)
294:             })
295:             .unwrap_or_else(|| self.provider.supports_thinking())
296:     }
297: 
298:     pub fn supports_tool_examples(&self) -> bool {
299:         self.supports_tool_examples_override
300:             .unwrap_or_else(|| self.family.supports_tool_examples())
301:     }
302: 
303:     /// A model supports fast mode exactly when it carries fast-tier pricing, so
304:     /// capability and billing can never disagree. Bedrock reuses
305:     /// `ProviderKind::Anthropic` and the same table, so we also gate on the
306:     /// provider here: fast mode only exists on the direct API.
307:     pub fn supports_fast(&self) -> bool {
308:         self.pricing.fast.is_some() && self.provider == ProviderKind::Anthropic
309:     }
310: 
311:     pub fn spec(&self) -> String {
312:         if let Some(slug) = &self.dynamic_slug {
313:             format!("{slug}/{}", self.id)
314:         } else {
315:             format!("{}/{}", self.provider, self.id)
316:         }
317:     }
318: 
319:     pub fn from_tier(provider: ProviderKind, tier: ModelTier) -> Result<Self, ModelError> {
320:         if let Some(spec) = crate::model_registry::model_registry()
321:             .read()
322:             .unwrap()
323:             .spec_for_tier(provider, tier)
324:         {
325:             return Self::from_spec(&spec);
326:         }
327:         let entries = models_for_provider(provider);
328:         let entry = entries
329:             .iter()
330:             .find(|e| e.default && e.tier == tier)
331:             .ok_or(ModelError::NoDefault(provider, tier))?;
332:         let model_id = entry.prefixes[0];
333:         Self::from_spec(&format!("{provider}/{model_id}"))
334:     }
335: 
336:     pub fn from_tier_dynamic(
337:         provider: ProviderKind,
338:         tier: ModelTier,
339:         dynamic_slug: Option<&str>,
340:     ) -> Result<Self, ModelError> {
341:         if let Some(slug) = dynamic_slug {
342:             if let Some(model) = dynamic::find_model_for_tier(slug, tier) {
343:                 return Ok(model);
344:             }
345:             if let Some(model) = super::providers::custom::find_model_for_tier(slug, tier) {
346:                 return Ok(model);
347:             }
348:             let mut model = Self::from_tier(provider, tier)?;
349:             model.dynamic_slug = Some(slug.to_string());
350:             return Ok(model);
351:         }
352:         Self::from_tier(provider, tier)
353:     }
354: 
355:     pub fn from_spec(spec: &str) -> Result<Self, ModelError> {
356:         let (provider_str, model_id) = spec.split_once('/').ok_or(ModelError::InvalidFormat)?;
357: 
358:         if let Ok(provider) = ProviderKind::from_str(provider_str) {
359:             return Ok(Self::from_base(provider, model_id, None));
360:         }
361: 
362:         if let Some(base) = dynamic::base_for_slug(provider_str) {
363:             if let Some(model) = dynamic::lookup_model(provider_str, model_id) {
364:                 return Ok(model);
365:             }
366:             return Ok(Self::from_base(base, model_id, Some(provider_str)));
367:         }
368: 
369:         if let Some(model) = super::providers::custom::lookup_model(provider_str, model_id) {
370:             return Ok(model);
371:         }
372: 
373:         Err(ModelError::UnsupportedProvider(provider_str.to_string()))
374:     }
375: }

419:     }
420: 
421:     pub fn cost(&self, pricing: &ModelPricing, fast: bool) -> f64 {
422:         let (input, output, cache_write, cache_read) = match &pricing.fast {
423:             Some(f) if fast => (
424:                 f.input,
425:                 f.output,
426:                 f.input * ModelPricing::CACHE_WRITE_MULTIPLIER,
427:                 f.input * ModelPricing::CACHE_READ_MULTIPLIER,
428:             ),
429:             _ => (
430:                 pricing.input,
431:                 pricing.output,
432:                 pricing.cache_write,
433:                 pricing.cache_read,
434:             ),
435:         };
436:         self.input as f64 * input / PER_MILLION
437:             + self.output as f64 * output / PER_MILLION
438:             + self.cache_creation as f64 * cache_write / PER_MILLION
439:             + self.cache_read as f64 * cache_read / PER_MILLION
440:     }
441: }
442: 
443: impl AddAssign for TokenUsage {
444:     fn add_assign(&mut self, rhs: Self) {
445:         self.input += rhs.input;
446:         self.output += rhs.output;
447:         self.cache_creation += rhs.cache_creation;
448:         self.cache_read += rhs.cache_read;
449:     }
450: }
```

```
244: pub struct Zai {
245:     compat: OpenAiCompatProvider,
246:     auth: Arc<Mutex<ResolvedAuth>>,
247:     key_pool: Option<KeyPool>,
248:     system_prefix: Option<String>,
249: }
250: 
251: impl Zai {
252:     pub fn new(timeouts: super::Timeouts) -> Result<Self, AgentError> {
253:         let pool = KeyPool::resolve("zai", CONFIG_STANDARD.api_key_env)?;
254:         let mut auth = ResolvedAuth::bearer(pool.current());
255:         let provider_config = maki_config::providers::ProvidersConfig::load();
256:         if let Some(url) =
257:             maki_config::providers::resolve_base_url("zai", provider_config.get("zai"))
258:         {
259:             auth.base_url = Some(url);
260:         }
261:         Ok(Self {
262:             compat: OpenAiCompatProvider::new(&CONFIG_STANDARD, timeouts),
263:             auth: Arc::new(Mutex::new(auth)),
264:             key_pool: Some(pool),
265:             system_prefix: None,
266:         })
267:     }
268: 
269:     pub(crate) fn with_auth(auth: Arc<Mutex<ResolvedAuth>>, timeouts: super::Timeouts) -> Self {
270:         Self {
271:             compat: OpenAiCompatProvider::new(&CONFIG_STANDARD, timeouts),
272:             auth,
273:             key_pool: None,
274:             system_prefix: None,
275:         }
276:     }
277: 
278:     pub(crate) fn with_system_prefix(mut self, prefix: Option<String>) -> Self {
279:         self.system_prefix = prefix;
280:         self
281:     }
282: }
283: 
284: impl Provider for Zai {
285:     fn stream_message<'a>(
286:         &'a self,
287:         model: &'a Model,
288:         messages: &'a [Message],
289:         system: &'a str,
290:         tools: &'a Value,
291:         event_tx: &'a Sender<ProviderEvent>,
292:         opts: RequestOptions,
293:         _session_id: Option<&str>,
294:     ) -> BoxFuture<'a, Result<StreamResponse, AgentError>> {
295:         Box::pin(async move {
296:             let auth = self.auth.lock().unwrap().clone();
297:             let mut buf = String::new();
298:             let system = super::with_prefix(&self.system_prefix, system, &mut buf);
299:             let mut body = self.compat.build_body(model, messages, system, tools);
300:             if model.supports_thinking() {
301:                 opts.thinking
302:                     .apply_reasoning_effort(&mut body, EffortScale::Glm);
303:             }
304:             match self
305:                 .compat
306:                 .do_stream(model, &[], &body, event_tx, &auth)
307:                 .await
308:             {
309:                 Err(AgentError::Api { status, message })
310:                     if (status == 429 || status >= 500)
311:                         && (message.contains("1113") || message.contains("nsufficien")) =>
312:                 {
313:                     warn!(status, "insufficient funds, bailing out");
314:                     Err(AgentError::Api {
315:                         status: 402,
316:                         message,
317:                     })
318:                 }
319:                 result => result,
320:             }
321:         })
322:     }
323: 
324:     fn list_models(&self) -> BoxFuture<'_, Result<Vec<crate::model::ModelInfo>, AgentError>> {
325:         Box::pin(async move {
326:             let auth = self.auth.lock().unwrap().clone();
327:             self.compat.do_list_models(&auth).await
328:         })
329:     }
330: 
331:     fn fetch_usage(&self) -> BoxFuture<'_, Result<Option<ProviderUsage>, AgentError>> {
332:         Box::pin(async move {
333:             let auth = self.auth.lock().unwrap().clone();
334:             let body = self.compat.get_text(&auth, QUOTA_LIMIT_URL).await?;
335:             let parsed: QuotaResponse = serde_json::from_str(&body)?;
336:             Ok(Some(parsed.into()))
337:         })
338:     }
339: 
340:     fn rotate_key(&self) -> BoxFuture<'_, Result<bool, AgentError>> {
341:         Box::pin(async {
342:             Ok(self
343:                 .key_pool
344:                 .as_ref()
345:                 .is_some_and(|p| p.rotate_auth(&self.auth, ResolvedAuth::bearer)))
346:         })
347:     }
348: 
349:     fn adjust_model(&self, model: &mut Model) {
350:         adjust_model(model);
351:     }
352: }
353: 
354: fn adjust_model(model: &mut Model) {
355:     if model.id.starts_with("glm-5.2") {
356:         model.supports_thinking_override = Some(true);
357:     }
358: }
```

### Assistant

Here is a structured summary of all provider-related changes between v0.3.23..v0.3.26.

---

## 1. Opencode provider (`maki-providers/src/providers/opencode.rs`) — entirely new (1228 lines)

**What it does:** A multi-provider router that discovers available models and their API endpoints from a remote catalog at `https://models.dev/api.json`. A single `opencode` provider slug can serve models hosted by _any_ third-party vendor (NVIDIA, Fireworks, Opencode itself, etc.) without hard-coding each one.

**Catalog-based model discovery:**

1. **`CatalogIndex`** (line 34) — JSON structure where keys are provider slugs (e.g. `"opencode"`, `"nvidia"`) and values are `CatalogProvider` descriptors containing:
   - `env` — list of env vars to try for an API key
   - `npm` — SDK package name (`@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` or `@ai-sdk/anthropic`), which determines wire format
   - `api` — optional base URL override
   - `models` — a `HashMap<String, CatalogModel>` of model IDs to their limits/costs

2. **`init_catalog_blocking()`** (line 563) — called once via `OnceLock` at construction:
   - Checks a local cache file (`models-dev-catalog.json` in the cache dir) with a 24-hour TTL
   - On cache miss, fetches from `CATALOG_URL` over HTTP
   - Deserializes into `CatalogData` via `catalog_to_data()` (line 468)

3. **`catalog_to_data()`** (line 468) — filters `CatalogIndex` into a flat `HashMap<(provider, model_id), CatalogMeta>`:
   - Only allows `ALLOWED_NPM` packages: `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` and `@ai-sdk/anthropic` (line 466)
   - Skips providers with no `api` URL
   - **Key filtering logic** (lines 486–506): a model is included only if `has_api_key` is true, **or** the model is free (zero-cost) under the `opencode` provider itself. A config flag `enable_free_models` gates whether free models appear at all (default false).
   - Builds `ResolvedAuth` per provider (API key via env var, `x-api-key` for Anthropic SDK, `Bearer` otherwise)

4. **Routing at inference** (`stream_message`, line 317): the model ID is split at `/` — the first segment is the sub-provider, the rest is the actual model ID. The `api_format` field (`ChatCompletions` vs `Messages`) determines which handler is called:
   - `handle_catalog_chat_completions` (line 235) — delegates to `OpenAiCompatProvider`
   - `handle_catalog_messages` (line 254) — uses Anthropic's `messages` API format with SSE parsing

**`ProviderKind::Opencode`** returns `&[]` for static model entries (`model.rs:198`) — all models come from the dynamic catalog.

**Key structs/functions:**
| Symbol | Line | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `CatalogProvider` | 37 | Provider descriptor from catalog JSON |
| `CatalogModel` | 83 | Model entry with limits, cost, shape |
| `CatalogMeta` | 120 | Resolved/processed metadata for a model |
| `CatalogData` | 133 | In-memory lookup table + auth map |
| `Opencode` | 195 | The provider impl |
| `init_catalog_blocking()` | 563 | One-time catalog init |
| `catalog_to_data()` | 468 | Filter/index builder |

---

## 2. Copilot auth flow (`maki-providers/src/providers/copilot/auth.rs`)

**Before v0.3.24:** `load_token()` would:
1. Check env vars `GH_COPILOT_TOKEN`/`COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`
2. Check saved credentials
3. Fall through to **auto-discover** tokens from `~/.config/github-copilot/hosts.json` or `~/.config/gh/hosts.yml` (gh CLI config)

`login()` just called `load_token()` — if a token existed anywhere (env, saved, **or** ambient gh config), it said "Copilot token found." No token was ever saved. `logout()` returned an error saying auth is managed externally.

**After v0.3.24 (commit `e163ed7`):**

- **`load_token()`** (line 20) now only checks env vars and saved credentials — **no longer falls through to file discovery**. Returns a clear error: "not authenticated, run `maki auth login copilot` or set `GH_COPILOT_TOKEN`"
- **`discover_token()`** (new function, line 41) — extracted into its own function. Scans the same files but is only called from `login()`.
- **`login(dir: &StateDir)`** — now explicitly:
  - Calls `load_token()` first (fast path if already authed)
  - Calls `discover_token()` to find tokens from gh/Copilot config
  - **Saves** the discovered token via `save_provider_credentials()` — so subsequent sessions find it in saved credentials
- **`logout(dir: &StateDir)`** — now actually deletes saved credentials instead of rejecting the operation
- Tests migrated from ad-hoc `#[test]` functions to `#[test_case]` parametrized tests (lines 132–152)

**Architectural implication:** Explicit login is now required. The ambient-gh-fallback is removed from request-path — auth is explicit, discoverable, and persistent.

---

## 3. Z.AI quota/monitor endpoint (`maki-providers/src/providers/zai/mod.rs`)

**New code added:**

**`QUOTA_LIMIT_URL`** (line 27): `https://api.z.ai/api/monitor/usage/quota/limit`

**Response types** (lines 29–50):
```rust
struct QuotaResponse { data: QuotaData }
struct QuotaData { limits: Vec<QuotaLimit>, level: Option<String> }
struct QuotaLimit { kind: String, unit: u32, percentage: u32, next_reset_time: Option<u64> }
```

**`quota_label()`** (line 52) — maps `(kind, unit)` pairs to human-readable labels:
- `("TOKENS_LIMIT", 3)` → "5-hour tokens"
- `("TOKENS_LIMIT", 6)` → "Weekly tokens"
- `("TIME_LIMIT", _)` → "Subscription time"
- Falls back to `"{kind} #{unit}"` for unknown units

**`impl From<QuotaResponse> for ProviderUsage`** (line 61) — converts API response into the generic `ProviderUsage` type.

**`fetch_usage()`** (line 331) — new trait method implementation: GETs the quota URL, parses JSON, returns `Some(ProviderUsage)`.

**Thinking support:**
- `stream_message()` (line 285) now accepts `opts: RequestOptions` (was `_opts`), and applies `opts.thinking.apply_reasoning_effort(&mut body, EffortScale::Glm)` when `model.supports_thinking()` (line 300–302)
- `adjust_model()` (line 354) — the `glm-5.2` model gets `supports_thinking_override = Some(true)` (line 356)
- New `BuiltInProvider` entry with two plans: `"standard"` (default model `glm-5.1`) and `"coding"` (default model `glm-5-code`), lines 80–109

---

## 4. Types (`maki-providers/src/types.rs`) — new types added

**`EffortScale` enum** (lines 301–312):
```rust
pub enum EffortScale {
    Standard,   // adaptive → "medium"
    PreferHigh, // adaptive → "high"
    HighOnly,   // always "high"
    Glm,        // off → "none", budget ≥8192 → "xhigh"
}
```
Previously `apply_reasoning_effort` took no scale argument — it always used "medium"/"low"/"high". Now each provider dialect passes a scale to get correct reasoning-effort strings. The `Glm` variant sends "none" for Off (GLM reasons by default, so "none" is explicit) and "xhigh" for budgets ≥8192.

**`apply_reasoning_effort()`** signature changed from `(self, body)` to `(self, body, scale: EffortScale)` at line 368.

**`apply_google_thinking()`** (line 389) — new method, sets `generationConfig.thinkingConfig`:
- Adaptive → `{"includeThoughts": true}`
- Budget → `{"thinkingBudget": n}`

**`apply_local_thinking()`** (line 401) — new method, sets `thinking_budget_tokens`:
- Off → `0`, Adaptive → `-1`, Budget → `n`

**`RequestOptions::clamped()`** (line 473) — new method:
- Strips `thinking` to `Off` if `model.supports_thinking()` is false
- Strips `fast` to `false` if `model.supports_fast()` is false
- Single gate for UI, restored sessions, and subagents

**`ProviderUsage` struct** (line 495):

```rust
    pub limits: Vec<UsageLimit>,
}
```

**`UsageLimit` struct** (line 504):

```rust
}
```

**`Message::first_text_content()`** changed from private `fn` to `pub fn` (line 219).

---

## 5. Model capabilities (`maki-providers/src/model.rs`)

**`supports_thinking_override: Option<bool>`** added to `Model` struct (line 225). This enables per-model thinking capability flags independent of the provider-level default.

**`Model::supports_thinking()`** (line 287):
```rust
pub fn supports_thinking(&self) -> bool {
    self.supports_thinking_override
        .unwrap_or_else(|| self.provider.supports_thinking())
}
```
Resolution order: override → discovered metadata → provider default.

**`ModelInfo`** gains `supports_thinking: Option<bool>` (line 58 of the struct definition) — so runtime-discovered models (from `/models` endpoints) can advertise thinking support.

**`ProviderKind::Opencode`** added to `models_for_provider()` returning `&[]` — the Opencode provider has no static model entries; all models come from the catalog (line 198).

**`TokenUsage`** gains `From`/`Into` conversions with `StoredTokenUsage` (lines 390–410) for session persistence.

**New tests** (lines 580–595):
- `opencode_from_spec_parses_four_levels` — `"opencode/nvidia/openai/gpt-oss-120b"` correctly splits into provider=`Opencode`, id=`"nvidia/openai/gpt-oss-120b"`
- `opencode_from_spec_parses_three_levels` — `"opencode/opencode/big-pickle"` works

**Architectural implication:** Thinking capability is now per-model rather than per-provider. The `clamped()` method on `RequestOptions` ensures that even if UI state or restored sessions have thinking enabled, it's disabled before the request goes out to a non-thinking model. Combined with `adjust_model()` hooks, individual models can be toggled on/off without changes to the provider trait.

---

### Cross-cutting architectural themes

1. **Thinking becomes per-model**: `supports_thinking_override` on `Model`, `EffortScale` per-provider dialect, `adjust_model()` on the provider trait.
2. **Usage quotas become a first-class concept**: `ProviderUsage`/`UsageLimit` types, `Provider::fetch_usage()` trait method, CLI `/usage` command in the UI.
3. **Opencode enables a catalog-of-providers pattern**: one provider slug routes to dozens of vendors dynamically, with API format auto-detection.
4. **Copilot auth becomes explicit**: no more ambient credentials — users must `maki auth login copilot` to import and persist the token.

```
448: impl<'de> Deserialize<'de> for PermissionsFileConfig {
449:     fn deserialize<D: serde::Deserializer<'de>>(deserializer: D) -> Result<Self, D::Error> {
450:         let table = toml::Table::deserialize(deserializer)?;
451:         let default = table
452:             .get("default")
453:             .and_then(|v| DefaultEffect::deserialize(v.clone()).ok())
454:             .or_else(|| {
455:                 table
456:                     .get("allow_all")?
457:                     .as_bool()?
458:                     .then_some(DefaultEffect::Allow)
459:             });
460: 
461:         let mut tools = HashMap::new();
462:         let mut mcp_rules = Vec::new();
463:         let mut mcp_defaults = HashMap::new();
464: 
465:         for (k, v) in table.iter() {
466:             if k.is_empty() || k == "allow_all" || k == "default" {
467:                 continue;
468:             }
469:             if k == "mcp" {
470:                 // TOML [mcp.server] creates nested table: mcp → {server → {...}}
471:                 if let Some(mcp_table) = v.as_table() {
472:                     for (server_name, server_value) in mcp_table {
473:                         if let Some(server_table) = server_value.as_table() {
474:                             parse_mcp_server_table(
475:                                 server_name,
476:                                 server_table,
477:                                 &mut mcp_rules,
478:                                 &mut mcp_defaults,
479:                             );
480:                         } else {
481:                             tracing::warn!(
482:                                 server = server_name.as_str(),
483:                                 "[mcp.{server_name}] is not a table — skipping"
484:                             );
485:                         }
486:                     }
487:                 } else {
488:                     tracing::warn!("[mcp] is not a table (got {}) — skipping", v.type_str());
489:                 }
490:             } else if let Ok(tp) = v.clone().try_into::<ToolPermissions>() {
491:                 if k.contains('.') {
492:                     tracing::warn!(
493:                         key = k.as_str(),
494:                         "tool section [{k}] contains a dot — did you mean [mcp.{k}]? Skipping."
495:                     );
496:                 } else {
497:                     tools.insert(k.clone(), tp);
498:                 }
499:             }
500:         }
501: 
502:         Ok(Self {
503:             default,
504:             tools,
505:             mcp_rules,
506:             mcp_defaults,
507:         })
508:     }
509: }
510:

556: use std::sync::Arc;
557: 
558: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
559: pub enum ToolKey {
560:     Wildcard,
561:     Native(Arc<str>),
562:     McpServer { server: Arc<str> },
563:     McpTool { server: Arc<str>, tool: Arc<str> },
564: }
565: 
566: /// NOTE: `ToolKey` deliberately does not implement `serde::Deserialize`.
567: /// Use `ToolKey::parse(&str)` at deserialization boundaries — it performs
568: /// validation (wire format, server name, length) that a blanket Deserialize
569: /// would skip. All current deserialization paths go through `parse`.
570: impl serde::Serialize for ToolKey {
571:     fn serialize<S: serde::Serializer>(&self, serializer: S) -> Result<S::Ok, S::Error> {
572:         serializer.collect_str(self)
573:     }
574: }
575: 
576: /// Check if a name matches the LLM wire format: `^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$`.
577: /// Tool names with dots, over 64 chars, or special characters are rejected.
578: pub fn is_valid_wire_name(name: &str) -> bool {
579:     !name.is_empty()
580:         && name.len() <= 64
581:         && name
582:             .bytes()
583:             .all(|b| b.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || b == b'-' || b == b'_')
584: }
585: 
586: impl ToolKey {
587:     /// Parse a qualified tool name into a `ToolKey`.
588:     ///
589:     /// Returns `Err` for malformed input (empty names, empty server/tool parts,
590:     /// tool names that don't match the wire format `^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$`).
591:     /// Use this at config/dispatch boundaries where input is untrusted.
592:     pub fn parse(name: &str) -> Result<Self, ToolKeyParseError> {
593:         if name.is_empty() {
594:             return Err(ToolKeyParseError::EmptyName);
595:         }
596:         if name == "*" {
597:             return Ok(Self::Wildcard);
598:         }
599:         match name.split_once('.') {
600:             Some(("", _)) | Some((_, "")) => {
601:                 Err(ToolKeyParseError::MalformedParts(name.to_string()))
602:             }
603:             Some((server, "*")) => {
604:                 if !is_valid_server_name(server) {
605:                     return Err(ToolKeyParseError::InvalidServerName(server.to_string()));
606:                 }
607:                 Ok(Self::McpServer {
608:                     server: server.into(),
609:                 })
610:             }
611:             Some((server, tool)) => {
612:                 if !is_valid_server_name(server) {
613:                     return Err(ToolKeyParseError::InvalidServerName(server.to_string()));
614:                 }
615:                 if !is_valid_wire_name(tool) {
616:                     return Err(ToolKeyParseError::InvalidToolName(tool.to_string()));
617:                 }
618:                 // Wire format is server__tool — check total length fits LLM API limits
619:                 let wire_len = server.len() + 2 + tool.len();
620:                 if wire_len > 64 {
621:                     return Err(ToolKeyParseError::WireNameTooLong {
622:                         server: server.to_string(),
623:                         tool: tool.to_string(),
624:                         len: wire_len,
625:                     });
626:                 }
627:                 Ok(Self::McpTool {
628:                     server: server.into(),
629:                     tool: tool.into(),
630:                 })
631:             }
632:             None => {
633:                 if !is_valid_wire_name(name) {
634:                     return Err(ToolKeyParseError::InvalidToolName(name.to_string()));
635:                 }
636:                 Ok(Self::Native(name.into()))
637:             }
638:         }
639:     }
640: 
641:     /// Create a `ToolKey` from a known-valid native tool name.
642:     ///
643:     /// # Panics
644:     ///
645:     /// Panics if `name` is empty or contains dots. Use `ToolKey::parse` for
646:     /// untrusted input or MCP tool names.
647:     pub fn native(name: &str) -> Self {
648:         match name {
649:             "*" => Self::Wildcard,
650:             _ => {
651:                 assert!(!name.is_empty(), "native tool name must not be empty");
652:                 assert!(
653:                     !name.contains('.'),
654:                     "native tool name must not contain dots: {name:?} - use ToolKey::parse for MCP tools"
655:                 );
656:                 Self::Native(name.into())
657:             }
658:         }
659:     }
660: 
661:     pub fn is_mcp(&self) -> bool {
662:         matches!(self, Self::McpServer { .. } | Self::McpTool { .. })
663:     }
664: }
665: 
666: impl std::fmt::Display for ToolKey {
667:     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
668:         match self {
669:             Self::Wildcard => write!(f, "*"),
670:             Self::Native(name) => write!(f, "{name}"),
671:             Self::McpServer { server } => write!(f, "{server}.*"),
672:             Self::McpTool { server, tool } => write!(f, "{server}.{tool}"),
673:         }
674:     }
675: }
676: 
677: /// Error returned when a tool key string fails validation.
678: #[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
679: pub enum ToolKeyParseError {
680:     #[error("tool name is empty")]
681:     EmptyName,
682:     #[error("malformed tool key: empty server or tool part in {0:?}")]
683:     MalformedParts(String),
684:     #[error("invalid server name {0:?}: must match [a-zA-Z0-9-]{{1,64}}")]
685:     InvalidServerName(String),
686:     #[error("invalid tool name {0:?}: must match [a-zA-Z0-9_-]{{1,64}}")]
687:     InvalidToolName(String),
688:     #[error("wire name {server}__{tool} is {len} chars, max 64")]
689:     WireNameTooLong {
690:         server: String,
691:         tool: String,
692:         len: usize,
693:     },
694: }

813:         ("index", Self::DEFAULT.index),
814:         ("grep", Self::DEFAULT.grep),

821:     fn from_file(f: Option<ToolOutputLinesFile>) -> Self {
822:         let d = Self::DEFAULT;
823:         let f = f.unwrap_or_default();
824:         Self {
825:             bash: f.bash.unwrap_or(d.bash),
826:             code_execution: f.code_execution.unwrap_or(d.code_execution),
827:             task: f.task.unwrap_or(d.task),
828:             index: f.index.unwrap_or(d.index),
829:             grep: f.grep.unwrap_or(d.grep),
830:             read: f.read.unwrap_or(d.read),
831:             write: f.write.unwrap_or(d.write),
832:             web: f.web.unwrap_or(d.web),
833:             other: f.other.unwrap_or(d.other),
834:         }
835:     }
836: 
837:     fn fields(&self) -> [(&'static str, usize); 9] {
838:         [
839:             ("bash", self.bash),
840:             ("code_execution", self.code_execution),
841:             ("task", self.task),
842:             ("index", self.index),
843:             ("grep", self.grep),
844:             ("read", self.read),
845:             ("write", self.write),
846:             ("web", self.web),
847:             ("other", self.other),
848:         ]
849:     }
850: 
851:     pub fn validate(&self) -> Result<(), ConfigError> {
852:         for (name, value) in self.fields() {
853:             check(
854:                 "ui.tool_output_lines",
855:                 name,
856:                 value as u64,
857:                 MIN_TOOL_OUTPUT_LINES as u64,
858:             )?;
859:         }
860:         Ok(())
861:     }
862: 
863:     pub fn get(&self, name: &str) -> usize {
864:         match name {
865:             "bash" => self.bash,
866:             "code_execution" => self.code_execution,
867:             "task" => self.task,
868:             "index" => self.index,
869:             "grep" | "glob" => self.grep,
870:             "read" => self.read,
871:             "memory" => self.write,
872:             name if FILE_WRITE_TOOLS.contains(&name) => self.write,
873:             "webfetch" | "websearch" => self.web,
874:             _ => self.other,
875:         }
876:     }
877: }

1057:     pub max_log_files: u32,
1058: 
1059:     #[config(default = DEFAULT_INPUT_HISTORY_SIZE, min = MIN_INPUT_HISTORY_SIZE,
1060:              desc = "Number of input history entries to retain")]
1061:     pub input_history_size: usize,
1062: }

1065:     fn default() -> Self {
1066:         Self {
1067:             max_log_bytes: DEFAULT_MAX_LOG_BYTES_MB * 1024 * 1024,
1068:             max_log_files: DEFAULT_MAX_LOG_FILES,
1069:             input_history_size: DEFAULT_INPUT_HISTORY_SIZE,
1070:         }
1071:     }

1078:             max_log_files: f.max_log_files.unwrap_or(DEFAULT_MAX_LOG_FILES),
1079:             input_history_size: f.input_history_size.unwrap_or(DEFAULT_INPUT_HISTORY_SIZE),

1084: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
1085: pub struct PluginsConfig {
1086:     pub enabled: bool,
1087:     pub tools: Vec<String>,
1088: }
1089: 
1090: impl PluginsConfig {
1091:     pub fn from_tools(tools: HashMap<String, ToolFileConfig>) -> Self {
1092:         let mut all: Vec<String> = DEFAULT_BUILTINS
1093:             .iter()
1094:             .filter(|name| tools.get(**name).and_then(|t| t.enabled).unwrap_or(true))
1095:             .map(|s| s.to_string())
1096:             .collect();
1097: 
1098:         let mut extra: Vec<&String> = tools
1099:             .iter()
1100:             .filter(|(name, cfg)| {
1101:                 !DEFAULT_BUILTINS.contains(&name.as_str()) && cfg.enabled.unwrap_or(false)
1102:             })
1103:             .map(|(name, _)| name)
1104:             .collect();
1105:         extra.sort();
1106:         all.extend(extra.into_iter().cloned());
1107: 
1108:         Self {
1109:             enabled: true,
1110:             tools: all,
1111:         }
1112:     }
1113: }

1115: impl Config {
1116:     pub fn validate(&self) -> Result<(), ConfigError> {
1117:         self.ui.validate_all()?;
1118:         self.agent.validate_all()?;
1119:         self.provider.validate()?;
1120:         self.storage.validate()?;
1121:         Ok(())
1122:     }
1123: }

1125: fn push_rules(
1126:     rules: &mut Vec<PermissionRule>,
1127:     tools: &HashMap<String, ToolPermissions>,
1128:     effect: Effect,
1129: ) {
1130:     for (tool, perms) in tools {
1131:         let scope_set = match effect {
1132:             Effect::Deny => &perms.deny,
1133:             Effect::Allow => &perms.allow,
1134:         };
1135:         let Some(scope_set) = scope_set else {
1136:             continue;
1137:         };
1138:         match scope_set {
1139:             ScopeSet::All(true) => rules.push(PermissionRule {
1140:                 tool: ToolKey::native(tool),
1141:                 scope: None,
1142:                 effect,
1143:             }),
1144:             ScopeSet::Scopes(scopes) => {
1145:                 for s in scopes {
1146:                     rules.push(PermissionRule {
1147:                         tool: ToolKey::native(tool),
1148:                         scope: Some(s.clone()),
1149:                         effect,
1150:                     });
1151:                 }
1152:             }
1153:             ScopeSet::All(false) => {}
1154:         }
1155:     }
1156: }
1157: 
1158: pub fn is_valid_server_name(name: &str) -> bool {
1159:     !name.is_empty()
1160:         && name.len() <= 64
1161:         && name.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || b == b'-')
1162: }
1163: 
1164: /// Validates the *tool* portion of an MCP qualified name.
1165: /// Currently identical to `is_valid_wire_name`, but kept distinct
1166: /// in case MCP tools need different constraints from native wire names.
1167: fn is_valid_tool_name(name: &str) -> bool {
1168:     is_valid_wire_name(name)
1169: }
1170: 
1171: fn push_mcp_tool_rule(
1172:     rules: &mut Vec<PermissionRule>,
1173:     server_name: &str,
1174:     tool_name: &str,
1175:     effect: Effect,
1176: ) {
1177:     let qualified = format!("{server_name}.{tool_name}");
1178:     match ToolKey::parse(&qualified) {
1179:         Ok(key) => {
1180:             rules.push(PermissionRule {
1181:                 tool: key,
1182:                 scope: None,
1183:                 effect,
1184:             });
1185:         }
1186:         Err(e) => {
1187:             tracing::warn!(
1188:                 server = server_name,
1189:                 tool = tool_name,
1190:                 error = %e,
1191:                 "skipping invalid MCP tool name"
1192:             );
1193:         }
1194:     }
1195: }
1196: 
1197: fn child_table<'a>(
1198:     table: &'a mut toml_edit::Table,
1199:     key: &str,
1200: ) -> Result<&'a mut toml_edit::Table, String> {
1201:     table
1202:         .entry(key)
1203:         .or_insert_with(|| toml_edit::Item::Table(toml_edit::Table::new()))
1204:         .as_table_mut()
1205:         .ok_or_else(|| format!("[{key}] is not a table"))
1206: }
1207: 
1208: fn push_unique(table: &mut toml_edit::Table, key: &str, value: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
1209:     let arr = table
1210:         .entry(key)
1211:         .or_insert_with(|| toml_edit::Item::Value(toml_edit::Value::Array(toml_edit::Array::new())))
1212:         .as_array_mut()
1213:         .ok_or_else(|| format!("{key} is not an array"))?;
1214:     if !arr.iter().any(|v| v.as_str() == Some(value)) {
1215:         arr.push(value);
1216:         arr.set_trailing("\n");
1217:         arr.set_trailing_comma(true);
1218:         for item in arr.iter_mut() {
1219:             item.decor_mut().set_prefix("\n    ");
1220:         }
1221:     }
1222:     Ok(())
1223: }
1224: 
1225: fn parse_mcp_server_table(
1226:     server_name: &str,
1227:     table: &toml::Table,
1228:     rules: &mut Vec<PermissionRule>,
1229:     mcp_defaults: &mut HashMap<ToolKey, DefaultEffect>,
1230: ) {
1231:     if !is_valid_server_name(server_name) {
1232:         tracing::warn!(
1233:             server = server_name,
1234:             "skipping [mcp.{server_name}] — invalid server name; \
1235:              must contain only alphanumeric characters and hyphens"
1236:         );
1237:         return;
1238:     }
1239: 
1240:     for (key, value) in table {
1241:         match key.as_str() {
1242:             "allow" | "deny" => {
1243:                 let effect = if key == "allow" {
1244:                     Effect::Allow
1245:                 } else {
1246:                     Effect::Deny
1247:                 };
1248:                 match value {
1249:                     toml::Value::Array(arr) => {
1250:                         for item in arr {
1251:                             if let Some(tool_name) = item.as_str() {
1252:                                 if tool_name == "*" {
1253:                                     // `allow = ["*"]` / `deny = ["*"]` means server-wide.
1254:                                     // Create an McpServer rule so deny-wins logic applies:
1255:                                     // McpServer deny blocks all tools on the server.
1256:                                     // No allow can override a deny — any deny wins.
1257:                                     rules.push(PermissionRule {
1258:                                         tool: ToolKey::McpServer {
1259:                                             server: server_name.into(),
1260:                                         },
1261:                                         scope: None,
1262:                                         effect,
1263:                                     });
1264:                                     continue;
1265:                                 }
1266:                                 push_mcp_tool_rule(rules, server_name, tool_name, effect);
1267:                             }
1268:                         }
1269:                     }
1270:                     toml::Value::Boolean(true) => {
1271:                         tracing::warn!(
1272:                             server = server_name,
1273:                             key = key.as_str(),
1274:                             "{key} = true is deprecated — use default = \"{key}\" instead; ignoring"
1275:                         );
1276:                     }
1277:                     toml::Value::Boolean(false) => {
1278:                         // No-op: explicitly disabled.
1279:                     }
1280:                     toml::Value::String(s) => {
1281:                         let tool_name = s.as_str();
1282:                         if tool_name == "*" {
1283:                             // Treat `allow = "*"` the same as `allow = ["*"]` —
1284:                             // create a hard McpServer rule, not a default.
1285:                             rules.push(PermissionRule {
1286:                                 tool: ToolKey::McpServer {
1287:                                     server: server_name.into(),
1288:                                 },
1289:                                 scope: None,
1290:                                 effect,
1291:                             });
1292:                         } else {
1293:                             tracing::info!(
1294:                                 server = server_name,
1295:                                 tool = tool_name,
1296:                                 "{key} = \"{tool_name}\" coerced to {key} = [\"{tool_name}\"] — \
1297:                                  consider using array syntax"
1298:                             );
1299:                             push_mcp_tool_rule(rules, server_name, tool_name, effect);
1300:                         }
1301:                     }
1302:                     other => {
1303:                         tracing::warn!(
1304:                             server = server_name,
1305:                             key = key.as_str(),
1306:                             value = ?other,
1307:                             "unexpected value for [mcp.{server_name}].{key} — \
1308:                              expected array of tool names or default = \"allow\"/\"deny\""
1309:                         );
1310:                     }
1311:                 }
1312:             }
1313:             "default" => {
1314:                 if let Ok(d) = value.clone().try_into::<DefaultEffect>() {
1315:                     mcp_defaults.insert(
1316:                         ToolKey::McpServer {
1317:                             server: server_name.into(),
1318:                         },
1319:                         d,
1320:                     );
1321:                 } else {
1322:                     tracing::warn!(
1323:                         server = server_name,
1324:                         value = ?value,
1325:                         "invalid [mcp.{server_name}].default value — expected \"allow\", \"deny\", or \"prompt\""
1326:                     );
1327:                 }
1328:             }
1329:             other => {
1330:                 if value.is_table() {
1331:                     tracing::warn!(
1332:                         server = server_name,
1333:                         key = other,
1334:                         "unknown key [mcp.{server_name}.{other}] — server names cannot \
1335:                          contain dots; use [mcp.{other}] instead if this is a server name"
1336:                     );
1337:                 } else {
1338:                     tracing::warn!(
1339:                         server = server_name,
1340:                         key = other,
1341:                         "unknown key in [mcp.{server_name}] — ignored"
1342:                     );
1343:                 }
1344:             }
1345:         }
1346:     }
1347: }
1348: 
1349: fn build_permissions(
1350:     global: PermissionsFileConfig,
1351:     project: PermissionsFileConfig,
1352: ) -> PermissionsConfig {
1353:     let global_default = global.default.unwrap_or(DefaultEffect::Prompt);
1354:     let default = match project.default {
1355:         Some(DefaultEffect::Allow) => global_default,
1356:         Some(d) => d,
1357:         None => global_default,
1358:     };
1359: 
1360:     let mut tool_defaults = HashMap::new();
1361:     for (tool, perms) in &global.tools {
1362:         if let Some(d) = perms.default {
1363:             let key = ToolKey::native(tool);
1364:             if matches!(key, ToolKey::Wildcard) {
1365:                 tracing::warn!(
1366:                     tool = tool,
1367:                     "ignoring [\"*\"].default — use the top-level `default` field instead \
1368:                      for global fallback behavior"
1369:                 );
1370:             } else {
1371:                 tool_defaults.insert(key, d);
1372:             }
1373:         }
1374:     }
1375:     for (key, d) in &global.mcp_defaults {
1376:         tool_defaults.insert(key.clone(), *d);
1377:     }
1378:     for (tool, perms) in &project.tools {
1379:         if let Some(d) = perms.default
1380:             && d != DefaultEffect::Allow
1381:         {
1382:             let key = ToolKey::native(tool);
1383:             if matches!(key, ToolKey::Wildcard) {
1384:                 tracing::warn!(
1385:                     tool = tool,
1386:                     "ignoring project [\"*\"].default — use the top-level `default` field instead"
1387:                 );
1388:             } else {
1389:                 tool_defaults.insert(key, d);
1390:             }
1391:         }
1392:     }
1393:     for (key, d) in &project.mcp_defaults {
1394:         if *d != DefaultEffect::Allow {
1395:             tool_defaults.insert(key.clone(), *d);
1396:         }
1397:     }
1398: 
1399:     let mut rules = Vec::new();
1400:     for rule in &global.mcp_rules {
1401:         if rule.effect == Effect::Deny {
1402:             rules.push(rule.clone());
1403:         }
1404:     }
1405:     for rule in &global.mcp_rules {
1406:         if rule.effect == Effect::Allow {
1407:             rules.push(rule.clone());
1408:         }
1409:     }
1410:     for tools in [&global.tools, &project.tools] {
1411:         push_rules(&mut rules, tools, Effect::Deny);
1412:         push_rules(&mut rules, tools, Effect::Allow);
1413:     }
1414:     for rule in &project.mcp_rules {
1415:         if rule.effect == Effect::Deny {
1416:             rules.push(rule.clone());
1417:         }
1418:     }
1419:     for rule in &project.mcp_rules {
1420:         if rule.effect == Effect::Allow {
1421:             rules.push(rule.clone());
1422:         }
1423:     }
1424:     PermissionsConfig {
1425:         default,
1426:         tool_defaults,
1427:         rules,
1428:         yolo: false,
1429:     }
1430: }
1431: 
1432: fn global_dir() -> Option<PathBuf> {
1433:     paths::config_dir().ok()
1434: }
1435: 
1436: fn config_search_dirs(global: Option<&Path>) -> Vec<PathBuf> {
1437:     let mut dirs = Vec::new();
1438:     if let Some(d) = global {
1439:         dirs.push(d.to_path_buf());
1440:     }
1441:     if let Ok(xdg) = paths::xdg_config_dir()
1442:         && dirs.first() != Some(&xdg)
1443:     {
1444:         dirs.push(xdg);
1445:     }
1446:     dirs
1447: }
1448: 
1449: fn load_env_files_with_global(cwd: &Path, global: Option<&Path>) {
1450:     let mut vars = HashMap::new();
1451:     if let Some(path) = global {
1452:         collect_env_vars(&path.join(".env"), &mut vars);
1453:     }
1454:     collect_env_vars(&cwd.join(PROJECT_DIR).join(".env"), &mut vars);
1455: 
1456:     for (key, value) in vars {
1457:         if std::env::var_os(&key).is_none() {
1458:             // SAFETY: single-threaded at startup, before any async runtime
1459:             unsafe { std::env::set_var(&key, &value) };
1460:         }
1461:     }
1462: }
1463: 
1464: fn collect_env_vars(path: &Path, vars: &mut HashMap<String, String>) {
1465:     let Ok(iter) = dotenvy::from_path_iter(path) else {
1466:         return;
1467:     };
1468:     for item in iter.flatten() {
1469:         vars.insert(item.0, item.1);
1470:     }
1471: }
1472: 
1473: pub fn load_env_files(cwd: &Path) {
1474:     load_env_files_with_global(cwd, global_dir().as_deref());
1475: }
1476: 
1477: pub fn load_permissions(cwd: &Path) -> PermissionsConfig {
1478:     let global_dirs = config_search_dirs(global_dir().as_deref());
1479:     load_permissions_inner(cwd, &global_dirs)
1480: }
1481: 
1482: fn load_permissions_inner(cwd: &Path, global_dirs: &[PathBuf]) -> PermissionsConfig {
1483:     let mut global_perms = PermissionsFileConfig::default();
1484:     for dir in global_dirs {
1485:         if let Some(p) = read_permissions_file(&dir.join(PERMISSIONS_FILE)) {
1486:             global_perms = p;
1487:         }
1488:     }
1489: 
1490:     let project_perms =
1491:         read_permissions_file(&cwd.join(PROJECT_DIR).join(PERMISSIONS_FILE)).unwrap_or_default();
1492: 
1493:     build_permissions(global_perms, project_perms)
1494: }
1495: 
1496: fn migrate_mcp_entry(
1497:     doc: &mut toml_edit::DocumentMut,
1498:     server_name: &str,
1499:     tool_name: &str,
1500:     item: &toml_edit::Item,
1501: ) {
1502:     // Old format: ["mcp:server__tool"] with booleans or scope-string arrays.
1503:     // New format: [mcp.server] allow = ["tool_name"]. Old scope strings were
1504:     // dead code (MCP scopes are always wildcarded), so only the effect survives.
1505:     let mut push = |effect_key: &str| {
1506:         let res = child_table(doc.as_table_mut(), "mcp")
1507:             .and_then(|mcp| child_table(mcp, server_name))
1508:             .and_then(|server| push_unique(server, effect_key, tool_name));
1509:         if let Err(e) = res {
1510:             warn!(
1511:                 server = server_name,
1512:                 tool = tool_name,
1513:                 error = %e,
1514:                 "skipping MCP entry migration"
1515:             );
1516:         }
1517:     };
1518: 
1519:     // Bare boolean: old format like [mcp]\ndeepwiki__search = true
1520:     // means "allow this tool".
1521:     if let Some(b) = item.as_bool() {
1522:         if b {
1523:             push("allow");
1524:         }
1525:         return;
1526:     }
1527: 
1528:     if let Some(old_table) = item.as_table() {
1529:         for (key, value) in old_table.iter() {
1530:             match key {
1531:                 "allow" | "deny" => {
1532:                     if value.as_bool() == Some(true) || value.as_array().is_some() {
1533:                         push(key);
1534:                     }
1535:                 }
1536:                 _ => {
1537:                     warn!(
1538:                         key,
1539:                         server = server_name,
1540:                         tool = tool_name,
1541:                         "dropping unknown key in old MCP entry during migration"
1542:                     );
1543:                 }
1544:             }
1545:         }
1546:     }
1547: }
1548: 
1549: /// Migrates old permission formats and returns the (possibly rewritten)
1550: /// file content. The rewrite to disk is best-effort: loading uses the
1551: /// migrated content even when the write fails.
1552: fn migrate_permissions_file(path: &Path) -> Option<String> {
1553:     let content = fs::read_to_string(path).ok()?;
1554:     let Ok(mut doc) = content.parse::<toml_edit::DocumentMut>() else {
1555:         return Some(content);
1556:     };
1557:     let mut migrated = false;
1558: 
1559:     if let Some(item) = doc.remove("allow_all") {
1560:         migrated = true;
1561:         if item.as_bool() == Some(true) {
1562:             doc.insert("default", toml_edit::value("allow"));
1563:         }
1564:     }
1565: 
1566:     // Migrate flat MCP keys: "mcp:server__tool" → [mcp.server]
1567:     // Two TOML representations to handle:
1568:     // 1. Quoted keys: ["mcp:server__tool"] → flat top-level key
1569:     // 2. Bare keys: [mcp:server__tool] → nested "mcp" → {"server__tool": ...}
1570: 
1571:     // Path 1: Flat quoted keys starting with "mcp:" containing "__"
1572:     let flat_old_keys: Vec<String> = doc
1573:         .iter()
1574:         .filter_map(|(k, _)| {
1575:             k.strip_prefix("mcp:")
1576:                 .and_then(|rest| rest.contains("__").then(|| k.to_string()))
1577:         })
1578:         .collect();
1579: 
1580:     for old_key in flat_old_keys {
1581:         if let Some(item) = doc.remove(&old_key) {
1582:             let rest = &old_key[4..]; // strip "mcp:"
1583:             if let Some((server, tool)) = rest.split_once("__") {
1584:                 if !is_valid_server_name(server) || !is_valid_tool_name(tool) {
1585:                     tracing::error!(
1586:                         key = old_key.as_str(),
1587:                         server = server,
1588:                         tool = tool,
1589:                         "SECURITY: skipping migration of malformed MCP key — \
1590:                          rules for this tool will not be restored"
1591:                     );
1592:                     continue;
1593:                 }
1594:                 migrate_mcp_entry(&mut doc, server, tool, &item);
1595:                 migrated = true;
1596:             }
1597:         }
1598:     }
1599: 
1600:     // Path 2: Nested "mcp" sub-table (bare key mcp: created nesting)
1601:     let nested_old_entries: Vec<(String, String, toml_edit::Item)> = {
1602:         let mut entries = Vec::new();
1603:         if let Some(toml_edit::Item::Table(mcp_table)) = doc.get("mcp") {
1604:             for (key, _) in mcp_table.iter() {
1605:                 if key.contains("__")
1606:                     && let Some((server, tool)) = key.split_once("__")
1607:                 {
1608:                     let item = mcp_table.get(key).cloned();
1609:                     if let Some(item) = item {
1610:                         entries.push((server.to_string(), tool.to_string(), item));
1611:                     }
1612:                 }
1613:             }
1614:         }
1615:         entries
1616:     };
1617: 
1618:     for (server_name, tool_name, item) in nested_old_entries {
1619:         if !is_valid_server_name(&server_name) || !is_valid_tool_name(&tool_name) {
1620:             tracing::error!(
1621:                 server = server_name.as_str(),
1622:                 tool = &*tool_name,
1623:                 "SECURITY: skipping migration of malformed nested MCP key — \
1624:                  rules for this tool will not be restored"
1625:             );
1626:             continue;
1627:         }
1628:         if let Some(toml_edit::Item::Table(mcp_table)) = doc.get_mut("mcp") {
1629:             mcp_table.remove(&format!("{server_name}__{tool_name}"));
1630:         }
1631:         migrate_mcp_entry(&mut doc, &server_name, &tool_name, &item);
1632:         migrated = true;
1633:     }
1634: 
1635:     // Clean up the now-empty "mcp" parent table if it has no children
1636:     if let Some(toml_edit::Item::Table(mcp_table)) = doc.get("mcp")
1637:         && mcp_table.is_empty()
1638:     {
1639:         doc.remove("mcp");
1640:     }
1641: 
1642:     if !migrated {
1643:         return Some(content);
1644:     }
1645:     let new_content = doc.to_string();
1646:     if let Err(e) = maki_storage::atomic_write(path, new_content.as_bytes()) {
1647:         warn!(path = %path.display(), error = %e, "failed to persist migrated permissions file");
1648:     }
1649:     Some(new_content)
1650: }
1651: 
1652: fn read_permissions_file(path: &Path) -> Option<PermissionsFileConfig> {
1653:     let content = migrate_permissions_file(path)?;
1654:     match toml::from_str(&content) {
1655:         Ok(p) => Some(p),

1671: pub fn append_permission_rule(
1672:     tool: &ToolKey,
1673:     scope: Option<&str>,
1674:     effect: Effect,
1675:     target: &PermissionTarget,
1676: ) -> Result<(), String> {
1677:     let dir = config_search_dirs(global_dir().as_deref())
1678:         .into_iter()
1679:         .last();
1680:     append_permission_rule_with_global(tool, scope, effect, target, dir)
1681: }
1682: 
1683: fn append_permission_rule_with_global(
1684:     tool: &ToolKey,
1685:     scope: Option<&str>,
1686:     effect: Effect,
1687:     target: &PermissionTarget,
1688:     global: Option<PathBuf>,
1689: ) -> Result<(), String> {
1690:     match target {
1691:         PermissionTarget::Global => append_global_permission(tool, scope, effect, global),
1692:         PermissionTarget::Project(cwd) => append_project_permission(tool, scope, effect, cwd),
1693:     }
1694: }
1695: 
1696: fn append_global_permission(
1697:     tool: &ToolKey,
1698:     scope: Option<&str>,
1699:     effect: Effect,
1700:     global: Option<PathBuf>,
1701: ) -> Result<(), String> {
1702:     let path = global
1703:         .ok_or_else(|| "cannot determine home directory".to_string())?
1704:         .join(PERMISSIONS_FILE);
1705:     let content = std::fs::read_to_string(&path).unwrap_or_default();
1706:     let mut doc: toml_edit::DocumentMut = content
1707:         .parse()
1708:         .map_err(|e| format!("failed to parse permissions: {e}"))?;
1709: 
1710:     insert_permission_entry(&mut doc, tool, scope, effect)?;
1711: 
1712:     if let Some(parent) = path.parent() {
1713:         std::fs::create_dir_all(parent).map_err(|e| format!("cannot create config dir: {e}"))?;
1714:     }
1715:     maki_storage::atomic_write(&path, doc.to_string().as_bytes())
1716:         .map_err(|e| format!("cannot write permissions: {e}"))?;
1717:     Ok(())
1718: }
1719: 
1720: fn append_project_permission(
1721:     tool: &ToolKey,
1722:     scope: Option<&str>,
1723:     effect: Effect,
1724:     cwd: &Path,
1725: ) -> Result<(), String> {
1726:     let path = cwd.join(PROJECT_DIR).join(PERMISSIONS_FILE);
1727:     let content = std::fs::read_to_string(&path).unwrap_or_default();
1728:     let mut doc: toml_edit::DocumentMut = content
1729:         .parse()
1730:         .map_err(|e| format!("failed to parse .maki/{PERMISSIONS_FILE}: {e}"))?;
1731: 
1732:     insert_permission_entry(&mut doc, tool, scope, effect)?;
1733: 
1734:     if let Some(parent) = path.parent() {
1735:         std::fs::create_dir_all(parent).map_err(|e| format!("cannot create .maki dir: {e}"))?;
1736:     }
1737:     maki_storage::atomic_write(&path, doc.to_string().as_bytes())
1738:         .map_err(|e| format!("cannot write .maki/{PERMISSIONS_FILE}: {e}"))?;
1739:     Ok(())
1740: }
1741: 
1742: fn insert_permission_entry(
1743:     doc: &mut toml_edit::DocumentMut,
1744:     tool_key: &ToolKey,
1745:     scope: Option<&str>,
1746:     effect: Effect,
1747: ) -> Result<(), String> {
1748:     let key = match effect {
1749:         Effect::Allow => "allow",
1750:         Effect::Deny => "deny",
1751:     };
1752: 
1753:     match tool_key {
1754:         // MCP scopes are always wildcarded, so `scope` is ignored for MCP keys.
1755:         ToolKey::McpTool { server, tool } => {
1756:             let server_table = child_table(child_table(doc.as_table_mut(), "mcp")?, server)?;
1757:             push_unique(server_table, key, tool)?;
1758:         }
1759:         ToolKey::McpServer { server } => {
1760:             let server_table = child_table(child_table(doc.as_table_mut(), "mcp")?, server)?;
1761:             server_table.insert("default", toml_edit::value(key));
1762:         }
1763:         ToolKey::Wildcard => {
1764:             // Wildcard rules are config-only; runtime never writes them.
1765:             return Err("cannot write wildcard permission rule to config".to_string());
1766:         }
1767:         ToolKey::Native(name) => {
1768:             let tool_table = child_table(doc.as_table_mut(), name)?;
1769:             match scope {
1770:                 Some(s) => push_unique(tool_table, key, s)?,
1771:                 None => {
1772:                     tool_table.insert(key, toml_edit::value(true));
1773:                 }
1774:             }
1775:         }
1776:     }
1777:     Ok(())
1778: }
```

```
418: impl<'de> Deserialize<'de> for PermissionsFileConfig {
419:     fn deserialize<D: serde::Deserializer<'de>>(deserializer: D) -> Result<Self, D::Error> {
420:         let table = toml::Table::deserialize(deserializer)?;
421:         let default = table
422:             .get("default")
423:             .and_then(|v| DefaultEffect::deserialize(v.clone()).ok())
424:             .or_else(|| {
425:                 table
426:                     .get("allow_all")?
427:                     .as_bool()?
428:                     .then_some(DefaultEffect::Allow)
429:             });
430:         let tools = table
431:             .iter()
432:             .filter(|(k, _)| k != &"allow_all" && k != &"default")
433:             .filter_map(|(k, v)| Some((k.clone(), v.clone().try_into::<ToolPermissions>().ok()?)))
434:             .collect();
435:         Ok(Self { default, tools })
436:     }
437: }

853: impl PluginsConfig {
854:     pub fn from_tools(tools: HashMap<String, ToolFileConfig>) -> Self {
855:         let mut all: Vec<String> = DEFAULT_BUILTINS
856:             .iter()

858:             .map(|s| s.to_string())
859:             .collect();
860: 
861:         let mut extra: Vec<&String> = tools
862:             .iter()

867:             .collect();

869:         all.extend(extra.into_iter().cloned());

873:             tools: all,
874:         }
875:     }

888: fn push_rules(
889:     rules: &mut Vec<PermissionRule>,
890:     tools: &HashMap<String, ToolPermissions>,
891:     effect: Effect,
892: ) {
893:     for (tool, perms) in tools {
894:         let scope_set = match effect {
895:             Effect::Deny => &perms.deny,
896:             Effect::Allow => &perms.allow,
897:         };
898:         let Some(scope_set) = scope_set else {
899:             continue;
900:         };
901:         match scope_set {
902:             ScopeSet::All(true) => rules.push(PermissionRule {
903:                 tool: tool.clone(),
904:                 scope: None,
905:                 effect,
906:             }),
907:             ScopeSet::Scopes(scopes) => {
908:                 for s in scopes {
909:                     rules.push(PermissionRule {
910:                         tool: tool.clone(),
911:                         scope: Some(s.clone()),
912:                         effect,
913:                     });
914:                 }
915:             }
916:             ScopeSet::All(false) => {}
917:         }
918:     }
919: }
920: 
921: fn build_permissions(
922:     global: PermissionsFileConfig,
923:     project: PermissionsFileConfig,
924: ) -> PermissionsConfig {
925:     let global_default = global.default.unwrap_or(DefaultEffect::Prompt);
926:     let default = match project.default {
927:         Some(DefaultEffect::Allow) => global_default,
928:         Some(d) => d,
929:         None => global_default,
930:     };
931: 
932:     let mut tool_defaults = HashMap::new();
933:     for (tool, perms) in &global.tools {
934:         if let Some(d) = perms.default {
935:             tool_defaults.insert(tool.clone(), d);
936:         }
937:     }
938:     for (tool, perms) in &project.tools {
939:         if let Some(d) = perms.default
940:             && d != DefaultEffect::Allow
941:         {
942:             tool_defaults.insert(tool.clone(), d);
943:         }
944:     }
945: 
946:     let mut rules = Vec::new();
947:     for tools in [&global.tools, &project.tools] {
948:         push_rules(&mut rules, tools, Effect::Deny);
949:         push_rules(&mut rules, tools, Effect::Allow);
950:     }
951:     PermissionsConfig {
952:         default,
953:         tool_defaults,
954:         rules,
955:         yolo: false,
956:     }
957: }
958: 
959: fn global_dir() -> Option<PathBuf> {
960:     paths::config_dir().ok()
961: }
962: 
963: fn config_search_dirs(global: Option<&Path>) -> Vec<PathBuf> {
964:     let mut dirs = Vec::new();
965:     if let Some(d) = global {
966:         dirs.push(d.to_path_buf());
967:     }
968:     if let Ok(xdg) = paths::xdg_config_dir()
969:         && dirs.first() != Some(&xdg)
970:     {
971:         dirs.push(xdg);
972:     }
973:     dirs
974: }
975: 
976: fn load_env_files_with_global(cwd: &Path, global: Option<&Path>) {
977:     let mut vars = HashMap::new();
978:     if let Some(path) = global {
979:         collect_env_vars(&path.join(".env"), &mut vars);
980:     }
981:     collect_env_vars(&cwd.join(PROJECT_DIR).join(".env"), &mut vars);
982: 
983:     for (key, value) in vars {
984:         if std::env::var_os(&key).is_none() {
985:             // SAFETY: single-threaded at startup, before any async runtime
986:             unsafe { std::env::set_var(&key, &value) };
987:         }
988:     }
989: }
990: 
991: fn collect_env_vars(path: &Path, vars: &mut HashMap<String, String>) {
992:     let Ok(iter) = dotenvy::from_path_iter(path) else {
993:         return;
994:     };
995:     for item in iter.flatten() {
996:         vars.insert(item.0, item.1);
997:     }
998: }
999: 
1000: pub fn load_env_files(cwd: &Path) {
1001:     load_env_files_with_global(cwd, global_dir().as_deref());
1002: }
1003: 
1004: pub fn load_permissions(cwd: &Path) -> PermissionsConfig {
1005:     let global_dirs = config_search_dirs(global_dir().as_deref());
1006:     load_permissions_inner(cwd, &global_dirs)
1007: }
1008: 
1009: fn load_permissions_inner(cwd: &Path, global_dirs: &[PathBuf]) -> PermissionsConfig {
1010:     let mut global_perms = PermissionsFileConfig::default();
1011:     for dir in global_dirs {
1012:         let path = dir.join(PERMISSIONS_FILE);
1013:         migrate_permissions_file(&path);
1014:         if let Some(p) = read_permissions_file(&path) {
1015:             global_perms = p;
1016:         }
1017:     }
1018: 
1019:     let project_path = cwd.join(PROJECT_DIR).join(PERMISSIONS_FILE);
1020:     migrate_permissions_file(&project_path);
1021:     let project_perms = read_permissions_file(&project_path).unwrap_or_default();
1022: 
1023:     build_permissions(global_perms, project_perms)
1024: }
1025: 
1026: fn migrate_permissions_file(path: &Path) {
1027:     let Ok(content) = fs::read_to_string(path) else {
1028:         return;
1029:     };
1030:     let Ok(mut doc) = content.parse::<toml_edit::DocumentMut>() else {
1031:         return;
1032:     };
1033:     let Some(item) = doc.remove("allow_all") else {
1034:         return;
1035:     };
1036:     if item.as_bool() == Some(true) {
1037:         doc.insert("default", toml_edit::value("allow"));
1038:     }
1039:     if let Err(e) = fs::write(path, doc.to_string()) {
1040:         warn!(path = %path.display(), error = %e, "failed to migrate permissions file");
1041:     }
1042: }
1043: 
1044: fn read_permissions_file(path: &Path) -> Option<PermissionsFileConfig> {
1045:     let content = fs::read_to_string(path).ok()?;
1046:     match toml::from_str(&content) {
1047:         Ok(p) => Some(p),
1048:         Err(e) => {
1049:             warn!(path = %path.display(), error = %e, "failed to parse permissions");
1050:             None
1051:         }
1052:     }
1053: }
1054: 
1055: pub fn global_config_dir() -> Option<PathBuf> {
1056:     global_dir()
1057: }
1058: 
1059: pub fn global_config_dirs() -> Vec<PathBuf> {
1060:     config_search_dirs(global_dir().as_deref())
1061: }
1062: 
1063: pub fn append_permission_rule(
1064:     tool: &str,
1065:     scope: Option<&str>,
1066:     effect: Effect,
1067:     target: &PermissionTarget,
1068: ) -> Result<(), String> {
1069:     let dir = config_search_dirs(global_dir().as_deref())
1070:         .into_iter()
1071:         .last();
1072:     append_permission_rule_with_global(tool, scope, effect, target, dir)
1073: }
1074: 
1075: fn append_permission_rule_with_global(
1076:     tool: &str,
1077:     scope: Option<&str>,
1078:     effect: Effect,
1079:     target: &PermissionTarget,
1080:     global: Option<PathBuf>,
1081: ) -> Result<(), String> {
1082:     match target {
1083:         PermissionTarget::Global => append_global_permission(tool, scope, effect, global),
1084:         PermissionTarget::Project(cwd) => append_project_permission(tool, scope, effect, cwd),
1085:     }
1086: }
1087: 
1088: fn append_global_permission(
1089:     tool: &str,
1090:     scope: Option<&str>,
1091:     effect: Effect,
1092:     global: Option<PathBuf>,
1093: ) -> Result<(), String> {
1094:     let path = global
1095:         .ok_or_else(|| "cannot determine home directory".to_string())?
1096:         .join(PERMISSIONS_FILE);
1097:     let content = std::fs::read_to_string(&path).unwrap_or_default();
1098:     let mut doc: toml_edit::DocumentMut = content
1099:         .parse()
1100:         .map_err(|e| format!("failed to parse permissions: {e}"))?;
1101: 
1102:     insert_permission_entry(&mut doc, tool, scope, effect)?;
1103: 
1104:     if let Some(parent) = path.parent() {
1105:         std::fs::create_dir_all(parent).map_err(|e| format!("cannot create config dir: {e}"))?;
1106:     }
1107:     std::fs::write(&path, doc.to_string()).map_err(|e| format!("cannot write permissions: {e}"))?;
1108:     Ok(())
1109: }
1110: 
1111: fn append_project_permission(
1112:     tool: &str,
1113:     scope: Option<&str>,
1114:     effect: Effect,
1115:     cwd: &Path,
1116: ) -> Result<(), String> {
1117:     let path = cwd.join(PROJECT_DIR).join(PERMISSIONS_FILE);
1118:     let content = std::fs::read_to_string(&path).unwrap_or_default();
1119:     let mut doc: toml_edit::DocumentMut = content
1120:         .parse()
1121:         .map_err(|e| format!("failed to parse .maki/{PERMISSIONS_FILE}: {e}"))?;
1122: 
1123:     insert_permission_entry(&mut doc, tool, scope, effect)?;
1124: 
1125:     if let Some(parent) = path.parent() {
1126:         std::fs::create_dir_all(parent).map_err(|e| format!("cannot create .maki dir: {e}"))?;
1127:     }
1128:     std::fs::write(&path, doc.to_string())
1129:         .map_err(|e| format!("cannot write .maki/{PERMISSIONS_FILE}: {e}"))?;
1130:     Ok(())
1131: }
1132: 
1133: fn insert_permission_entry(
1134:     doc: &mut toml_edit::DocumentMut,
1135:     tool: &str,
1136:     scope: Option<&str>,
1137:     effect: Effect,
1138: ) -> Result<(), String> {
1139:     let key = match effect {
1140:         Effect::Allow => "allow",
1141:         Effect::Deny => "deny",
1142:     };
1143: 
1144:     let tool_table = doc
1145:         .entry(tool)
1146:         .or_insert_with(|| toml_edit::Item::Table(toml_edit::Table::new()));
1147:     let tool_table = tool_table
1148:         .as_table_mut()
1149:         .ok_or_else(|| format!("[{tool}] is not a table"))?;
1150: 
1151:     match scope {
1152:         Some(s) => {
1153:             let arr = tool_table.entry(key).or_insert_with(|| {
1154:                 toml_edit::Item::Value(toml_edit::Value::Array(toml_edit::Array::new()))
1155:             });
1156:             let arr = arr
1157:                 .as_array_mut()
1158:                 .ok_or_else(|| format!("[{tool}].{key} is not an array"))?;
1159:             let already_exists = arr
1160:                 .iter()
1161:                 .any(|v| v.as_str().is_some_and(|existing| existing == s));
1162:             if !already_exists {
1163:                 arr.push(s);
1164:                 arr.set_trailing("\n");
1165:                 arr.set_trailing_comma(true);
1166:                 for item in arr.iter_mut() {
1167:                     item.decor_mut().set_prefix("\n    ");
1168:                 }
1169:             }
1170:         }
1171:         None => {
1172:             tool_table.insert(key, toml_edit::value(true));
1173:         }
1174:     }
1175:     Ok(())
1176: }

1379:         let err = config.validate().unwrap_err();

1638:     #[test]
1639:     fn env_file_precedence() {
1640:         const GLOBAL_ONLY: &str = "TEST_MAKI_GLOBAL_ONLY";
1641:         const PROJECT_SHADOWS: &str = "TEST_MAKI_PROJECT_SHADOWS";
1642:         const PROCESS_WINS: &str = "TEST_MAKI_PROCESS_WINS";
1643: 
1644:         let dir = TempDir::new().unwrap();
1645:         let global = global_config_dir(dir.path());
1646:         fs::create_dir_all(&global).unwrap();
1647:         fs::write(
1648:             global.join(".env"),
1649:             format!("{GLOBAL_ONLY}=global\n{PROJECT_SHADOWS}=global\n{PROCESS_WINS}=global"),
1650:         )
1651:         .unwrap();

1653:         let maki_dir = dir.path().join(".maki");
1654:         fs::create_dir_all(&maki_dir).unwrap();
1655:         fs::write(
1656:             maki_dir.join(".env"),
1657:             format!("{PROJECT_SHADOWS}=project\n{PROCESS_WINS}=project"),
1658:         )
1659:         .unwrap();
1660:
```

```
395:         KeyCode::Home => "Home".to_string(),
396:         KeyCode::End => "End".to_string(),
397:         KeyCode::PageUp => "PageUp".to_string(),
398:         KeyCode::PageDown => "PageDown".to_string(),
399:         KeyCode::Insert => "Insert".to_string(),
400:         KeyCode::F(n) => format!("F{}", n),
401:         _ => "".to_string(),
402:     };
403:     label_parts.push(&key_name);
404:     let label = label_parts.join("+");
405: 
406:     Some(Bind {
407:         code,
408:         modifiers,
409:         label: Box::leak(label.into_boxed_str()),
410:         name: None,
411:     })
412: }
413: 
414: pub fn update_bind(action: &str, bind_str: &str) -> bool {
415:     if let Some(mut bind) = parse_keybind(bind_str) {
416:         let binds = CURRENT_BINDS.get_or_init(|| std::sync::RwLock::new(ConfiguredKeybindings::default()));
417:         if let Ok(mut write) = binds.write() {
418:             bind.name = Some(Box::leak(action.to_string().into_boxed_str()));
419:             match action {
420:                 "quit" => write.quit = bind,
421:                 "help" => write.help = bind,
422:                 "prev_chat" => write.prev_chat = bind,
423:                 "next_chat" => write.next_chat = bind,
424:                 "scroll_half_up" => write.scroll_half_up = bind,
425:                 "scroll_half_down" => write.scroll_half_down = bind,
426:                 "scroll_line_up" => write.scroll_line_up = bind,
427:                 "scroll_line_down" => write.scroll_line_down = bind,
428:                 "scroll_top" => write.scroll_top = bind,
429:                 "scroll_bottom" => write.scroll_bottom = bind,
430:                 "pop_queue" => write.pop_queue = bind,
431:                 "delete_word" => write.delete_word = bind,
432:                 "search" => write.search = bind,
433:                 "file_picker" => write.file_picker = bind,
434:                 "toggle_verbose" => write.toggle_verbose = bind,
435:                 "open_editor" => write.open_editor = bind,
436:                 "edit_system_prompt" => write.edit_system_prompt = bind,
437:                 "plan_toggle" => write.plan_toggle = bind,
438:                 "tasks" => write.tasks = bind,
439:                 "suspend" => write.suspend = bind,
440:                 "delete" => write.delete = bind,
441:                 "kill_line" => write.kill_line = bind,
442:                 "line_start" => write.line_start = bind,
443:                 "line_end" => write.line_end = bind,
444:                 "edit_input" => write.edit_input = bind,
445:                 "sessions" => write.sessions = bind,
446:                 "shift_session_down" => write.shift_session_down = bind,
447:                 "shift_session_up" => write.shift_session_up = bind,
448:                 _ => return false,
449:             }
450:             return true;
451:         }
452:     }
453:     false
454: }

600: impl Platform {
```
